papers.title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
papers.abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

papers.title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
papers.abstract: Post-stroke aphasia is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional classifications may not capture differences in brain functional organisation. We tested whether resting-state and task-based functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) could identify neurophysiological subgroups alongside clinical this http URL -nine patients underwent unsupervised clustering using three fNIRS feature views: resting-state activity and connectivity, language-task activation, and rest-to-task connectivity reconfiguration. Similarity network fusion and spectral clustering integrated the views. Clinical and behavioural measures were excluded from this http URL clusters (n = 32, 17 and 30) were identified. This solution had the largest eigengap and was the only candidate significant after permutation testing and Holm correction (adjusted P = 0.001). It was stable under subsampling (mean adjusted Rand index, 0.773), but agreement fell to 0.217 when the resting-state view was removed. Clusters differed in most regional intrinsic-activity measures and all resting-state connectivity summaries, with few differences in task activation or connectivity reconfiguration. Their profiles showed higher right anterior prefrontal activity, distributed fronto-sensorimotor and parietal alterations, and reduced interhemispheric connectivity, this http URL membership was not significantly associated with conventional aphasia subtype (Cramér's V = 0.287), and baseline clinical language scores and task performance did not differ between this http URL findings identify three neurophysiological subgroups distinguished mainly by intrinsic activity and resting-state functional connectivity, not clearly aligned with conventional aphasia classifications or baseline clinical measures. Multi-view fNIRS analysis may complement clinical characterisation, requiring independent and longitudinal validation.

papers.title: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful
papers.abstract: Single-cell-informed deconvolution provides cell-type-resolved features for clinical bulk RNA cohorts. Most existing methods predict the proportions $\pi_k$ of the $K$ constituent cell types (CTs). Fewer predict cell-type-specific expression (CTSE) $\mu_{kg}$ of gene $g$ in CT $k$, which can capture cell states that proportions miss, but recent benchmarks find it much harder. We explain this gap with closed-form accuracy bounds. For CTSE, we derive an $R^2$ ceiling for per-gene linear estimators. For proportions, the best linear estimator, which pools evidence across genes, has a closed-form $R^2$, and a computable lower bound on it predicts which CTs are learnable. We study targeted deconvolution of 106 biologically curated (CT, gene) pairs, found post hoc to have higher learnability scores. On overall survival in non-small cell lung cancer, estimation difficulty does not predict prognostic value across these targets. Yet a sparse survival model on deconvolved features, mostly CTSE, predicts survival as well as a sparse model on the bulk genes themselves, while attributing its signal to specific cell types. Some deconvolved CTSE features reveal prognostic signal not seen in the corresponding bulk gene.

papers.title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
papers.abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.

papers.title: When High Capacity Becomes Undeployable: Pore-Filling Constraints for Multi-Objective Optimization of Direct Air Capture Sorbents
papers.abstract: Amine-impregnated sorbents with the highest nominal CO2 capacity are frequently the least deployable, as amine beyond the pore-volume limit blocks active sites. Yet multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) for direct air capture (DAC) treats formulation search as unconstrained. We encode the pore-filling boundary as an explicit outcome constraint, c(x) = tanh(1 - phi_hat) - tau, and use it as a diagnostic instrument on a hand-curated, DOI-traceable benchmark of 618 solid-amine formulations from 43 publications. Unconstrained MOBO attains higher nominal capacity (3.639 +/- 0.815 vs. 2.964 +/- 0.728 mmol/g, p = 1.0e-11), but across 100 seeds 63.2% of its Pareto-optimal candidates violate the pore-filling boundary versus 39.3% under the constraint: it is rewarded for proposing candidates outside the pore-confined design regime. The constraint steers the front to lower loadings (55.8 vs. 65.2 wt%) and larger pores. The boundary is corroborated once apparatus effects are harmonized hierarchically: 77.8% of kinetic variance is between-laboratory, and pore filling carries a significant kinetic penalty (p = 0.002). Standard hypervolume over-credits feasibility-agnostic methods by 13.9-16.1% (vs. 11.1% constrained), and three surrogate-based analyses---the constrained front, a regeneration-energy third objective, and harmonized kinetics---consistently point to a conservative deployable window at pore filling phi_hat ~ 0.4-0.5 (45-55 wt% loading). The benchmark and associated analysis outputs accompany this submission.

papers.title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
Nontrivial criticality and weakly first-order transitions in the frustrated spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy
papers.abstract: Frustrated spin chains host exotic phases beyond the Landau paradigm, yet weak first-order transitions and unconventional criticalities remain elusive. Combining large-scale density-matrix renormalization group with bosonization methods, we map the phase diagram of a spin-1 chain with next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) coupling and single-ion anisotropy (SIA). We pinpoint two topological phase transitions: a weakly first-order transition between the Haldane and NNN-Haldane phases with a tiny gap and a continuous transition from the Haldane phase to the large-$D$ phase located via level spectroscopy with Richardson extrapolation. For negative SIA, a spontaneous dimerized phase emerges between the Néel and NNN-Néel phases. Its transition into the Néel phase is a deconfined quantum critical point falling into the eight-vertex universality class, with central charge $c = 1$ and critical exponents varying continuously along the phase boundary. For positive SIA, we identify two vector-spin-chirality orders---an ordinary chiral phase and a narrow Haldane-chiral phase---with a weakly first-order transition between them, evidenced by a soft jump in the string order parameter. Our results reveal that frustration and anisotropy generate emergent orders and non-Landau criticalities, providing a platform for deconfined and topological phase transitions.

papers.title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
papers.abstract: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $\phi_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $\phi_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.

papers.title: Quantum Metric Connects Bond Delocalization to Phonon Softening
papers.abstract: Delocalized bonding electrons have long been associated with soft bonds and low phonon frequencies. However, a quantitative connection between electron delocalization and phonon softening remains elusive. We identify such a connection through the momentum-space quantum metric, which measures the intrinsic delocalization of the occupied electronic states. We show that a quantum geometric contribution to phonon softening is proportional to the integrated quantum metric. First-principles calculations of more than a hundred compounds demonstrate that greater quantum metric generally accompanies softer phonons. Localized Wannier orbitals reveal the bonding environments associated with this delocalization. In ferroelectric GeTe, LiBeSb, and BaTiO$_3$, polar distortion localizes the bonding orbitals, reduces quantum metric, and stabilizes the soft mode of the nonpolar structure. In PbSe, pressure-induced band inversion is accompanied by an enhanced quantum metric and phonon softening without change in crystal symmetry and bonding. These results establish a common quantum geometric interpretation of bond delocalization and phonon softening across distinct bonding environments.

papers.title: Tunable quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect in the PT-symmetric sliding antiferroelectric MoS$_2$
papers.abstract: The quantum metric, the real part of a quantum geometric tensor, plays an important role in fundamental transport and optical responses of quantum materials. While net quantum metric effects are typically realized by breaking both time-reversal (T) and inversion (P) symmetries, valley-contrast mechanisms enable the probing of quantum geometry in centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic systems, revealing physical signatures beyond Berry curvature. Here, we design a four-layer MoS$_2$ platform that combines sliding antiferroelectric order with strain-induced $C_{3z}$ breaking to realize a quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect (NVHE) under preserved P and T symmetries. Reversible interlayer sliding (ABBA $\leftrightarrow$ BAAB) provides nonvolatile electrical control of the valley response. First-principles calculations reveal an outer-layer-dominated NVHE with tunable sign and magnitude. This symmetry-preserving, sliding-tunable strategy activates hidden quantum geometric phenomena in realistic two-dimensional materials and opens a clean pathway for tunable valleytronics and quantum information devices.

papers.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics
papers.abstract: Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gröbner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators. An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.

papers.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
papers.abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

papers.title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
papers.abstract: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity. We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon). Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

papers.title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
papers.abstract: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions. We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

papers.title: Quantum Geometric Origin of Néel-Order-Driven Magneto-Optical Response in MnTe
papers.abstract: Magneto-optical (MO) responses provide a direct probe of magnetic order, yet resolving compensated antiferromagnetic order remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in altermagnetic MnTe that the symmetry of the Néel order is imprinted on the MO response through distinct quantum-geometric contributions. Combining first-principles calculations with a Landau symmetry framework, we demonstrate that the quantum metric gives rise to a twofold optical anisotropy, with its diagonal and symmetric off-diagonal components forming an $E_{2g}$ doublet associated with the quadratic Néel-order invariants, providing a characteristic MO Voigt signature of the Néel-vector orientation. In contrast, the Berry curvature generates a complementary threefold Hall response governed by the cubic $A_{2g}$ Néel-order invariant. Although the Hall conductivity and the out-of-plane weak-ferromagnetic moment share the same symmetry and angular dependence, constraining the latter to zero leaves the optical Hall response essentially unchanged demonstrating that the Hall response originates directly from the compensated Néel order rather than the net magnetization. Our results establish quantum geometry as a direct link between Néel order and MO response, revealing distinct twofold and threefold optical signatures of Néel order in altermagnetic MnTe.

papers.title: Frustration in system with intercalated and bilayer smectic structure
papers.abstract: The dimeric mesogens exhibit an unusual variety of mesophases - nematic and smectic, with distinctly different packing schemes. The relation between molecular and mesophase structure was studied for homologue series of non-symmetric bent dimers this http URL , obtained by serial Pd- and Pt-catalyzed cross-coupling chemical reactions. The shorter homologues of the series form smectics with an intercalated structure, and longer homologues form bilayer smectics with broken up-down symmetry of molecular orientation within the layers, for intermediate homologues frustration leads to a nematic gap. The additional structure complexity arises from the tendency of bent dimers to form twisted structures, in which the azimuthal angle of tilted molecules forms both short- and long-pitch helices. Here we confirm, through resonant X-ray diffraction, that longer homologues form a helical four-layer structure of SmCTB-SH phase, along with a more complex one in which, in addition to the basic four-layer unit, an extra helix is superimposed, SmCTB-DH phase. This additional helix has a periodicity that is strongly temperature-dependent; upon cooling, it changes from 100 nm to 40 nm.

papers.title: Toward a quantum resistance standard above liquid nitrogen temperature
papers.abstract: Quantum Hall effect (QHE) -- the pioneering demonstration of one-dimensional topologically-protected edge channels -- manifest a transversal resistance quantized solely by two universal constants $e$ and $h$ (the elementary charge and the Planck constant, respectively), referred to as the von Klitzing constant $R_\mathrm{K}=h/e^{2}$. For decades, this has enabled a unique route for realizing quantum Hall resistance (QHR) standard in the Système international d'unitès (SI), yet high precision QHR under relaxed conditions, especially temperature higher than 30 K, has not been possible. Here, we show that interfacial charge-order coupling inbetween CrOCl and monolayer graphene offers enhanced Fermi velocity, creating a robust Landau cyclotron gap. Using a customized direct current comparator (DCC, mounted at room temperature), we obtain relative deviation of the Hall resistance from $R_\mathrm{K}/2$ of (15 $\pm$ 23)\,n$\Omega$ $\Omega$$^{-1}$ (23 parts per billion of relative uncertainty) at 50 K, with an external magnetic field of 12 T and a dc current of 10 $\mu$A. At 100 K, the system exhibits QHR with 2 parts per million of relative uncertainty. Our results therefore suggest a platform toward a next-generation quantum resistance standard that may work at above liquid nitrogen temperature and free of conventional compressor refrigerators.

papers.title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
papers.abstract: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

papers.title: Towards Quark-Gluon Correlations in Pion from the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
papers.abstract: Twist-3 distributions encode quark-gluon correlations, and the pion's chiral-odd $e(x)$ is the simplest of them. QCD fixes its lowest moments exactly, yet the only rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of $e(x)$ omitted the Wilson line and violated the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment. We show that the discrepancy is not a failure of RL but of the omitted link: at first order in the coupling, the link contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel the EOM violation class by class, so the sum rule is restored exactly in RL. The resulting zeroth and first moments are complete RL results. The genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$, and the Wilson line more than doubles its magnitude in the negative region. This identifies the Wilson line as the missing ingredient in the RL description of $e(x)$ and sets the stage for a full resummation of the $gA$ expansion.

papers.title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
Non-perturbative charm production from color ropes in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract: We present results on charm production in nucleus-nucleus reactions in the energy range $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5$-$20$ GeV, obtained with the SMASH transport approach extended to include color rope formation. We show that string fusion may provide a substantial additional non-perturbative source of charm production. This may help to explain the apparent charm enhancement (above the pQCD expectations) at low transverse momenta. Our predicted neutral $D$-meson yields are consistent with current experimental constraints and may provide valuable insights for upcoming data by the NA61/SHINE collaboration.

papers.title: Determining the kaon distribution amplitudes by fitting the $D\to K$ transition form factor to investigate the equivalence of two chiral LCSR frameworks
papers.abstract: In this work, we fit the $D\to K$ vector transition form factor (TFF) to the BESIII experimental data using a Monte Carlo (MC) method. We also calculate the TFF using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) with left-and right-handed chiral currents. For the TFF derived using the right-handed chiral current, the key input is the kaon twist-2 distribution amplitude (DA), for which we consider three models: the power-law parametrization ($\mathrm{R1}$), the truncated Gegenbauer expansion ($\mathrm{R2}$), and the light-cone harmonic oscillator (LCHO) model ($\mathrm{R3}$). The parameters of these models are determined by fitting the corresponding TFF predictions to the MC-fit results. For the TFF derived using the left-handed chiral current, the dominant input is the kaon twist-3 DA ($\mathrm{L4}$), which is constructed within the LCHO framework. Its parameters are determined from theoretical constraints rather than from the fit. In the large-recoil region, the resulting TFF are $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R1}}=0.7381^{+0.0180}_{-0.0194}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R2}}=0.7320^{+0.0178}_{-0.0192}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R3}}=0.7324^{+0.0180}_{-0.0191}$, and $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{L4}}=0.7343^{+0.0459}_{-0.0573}$. We then calculate the decay widths and branching fractions of the semileptonic decays $D\to K e\nu_e$ and extract the CKM matrix element $|V_{cs}|$. Finally, we predict the two important ratios, $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^-/K^-}^{e}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^0/K^0}^{e}$. All the obtained results are consistent with existing experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Discrete truncated Wigner approximation of the quantum phase transition in the transverse-field Ising model
papers.abstract: The discrete truncated Wigner approximation (DTWA) has been a workhorse for large-scale spin dynamics, but whether it captures dynamics across a quantum phase transition has not been tested systematically. In this work, we use the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) to study the quantum phase transition with DTWA from one to three dimensions and with all-to-all connectivity, using slow linear ramps and fast ramps. We find that DTWA cannot capture the dynamics on the one-dimensional chain, and that its behavior is consistent with classical thermalization, in which its classical spins relax toward a thermal state at a finite effective temperature that does not vanish for slow ramps, while a one-dimensional chain cannot order at any finite temperature. For square and cubic lattices, in contrast to the chain, DTWA builds order, and the order sets in close to the quantum critical point found by quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). However, its correlations do not grow with the Kibble-Zurek exponents, so DTWA captures the onset of order but not the universal dynamics of the transition. For all-to-all coupling, DTWA follows the exact growth of the order parameter along the entire ramp. Our results suggest that DTWA becomes more reliable as each spin interacts with more partners, and that beyond one dimension it can indicate where a quantum phase transition lies but cannot capture its critical scaling.

papers.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
papers.abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $\lambda$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 Å$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 Å$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.

papers.title: Rotation curves of dwarf galaxies and dark matter as a condensate of $q$-deformed bosons: reconstruction and fits of the deformation profile
papers.abstract: Dark-matter-dominated dwarf galaxies are a sensitive testing ground for models in which dark matter is a self-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). In the Thomas-Fermi limit the standard BEC halo has the density profile $\rho\propto\sin(kr)/(kr)$, so that the shape of its rotation curve is fixed up to two scale parameters. Here we consider a condensate of $q$-deformed bosons. We show that, in the Thomas-Fermi limit, the deformation enters the structure of the halo only through the chemical potential of the condensate; consequently, a spatially uniform deformation parameter leaves the standard BEC profile unchanged. In every galaxy $\chi$ is depressed in the inner region, $kr\lesssim1$, relative to the outer halo, where it is approximately constant in most cases: the standard condensate describes the outer halo, while the core requires a weaker deformation, i.e., $q$ closer to unity. The profiles share this qualitative shape, but neither the depth nor the width of the depression is universal. Modelling the depression by a Gaussian, with two additional parameters, we fit the rotation curves with rms residuals of $0.6$--$2.6$~km\,s$^{-1}$, against $1.6$--$8.5$~km\,s$^{-1}$ for the standard condensate. According to the Bayesian information criterion, the deformed condensate is preferred over the standard condensate, the Navarro-Frenk-White profile, and the Burkert profile in four galaxies, is indistinguishable from the best of them in two, and is disfavoured in two. We discuss the limitations of these results, in particular the absence of error bars in the data, the neglect of baryons, and the phenomenological status of a position-dependent deformation.

papers.title: Milk-removal feedback shapes lactation sustainability and daily output in a model of human lactation
papers.abstract: Milk production during lactation is dynamically regulated by milk removal, yet quantitative models linking feeding or pumping schedules to subsequent production remain scarce. We develop a minimal model describing milk accumulation and production between removal sessions, and the stimulation of subsequent production through milk removal. We compare different assumptions about how stimulation depends on the amount of milk removed or the duration of removal, and consider two removal protocols: prescribing either the removed amount or the removal duration. When stimulation depends on the removed amount, declining production can reduce subsequent stimulation and reinforce the decline. This leads to a critical wait interval beyond which no repeated constant schedule can sustain lactation. If stimulation is inefficient for small removal amounts but more efficient at intermediate amounts, the model can exhibit bistability: depending on the initial conditions, milk production either persists or ceases. In contrast, duration-dependent stimulation does not permit a zero-production state under continued removal, but can generate non-constant long-term dynamics under certain conditions. We further show that maximizing milk removal per session need not maximize daily output, because increased removal competes with session frequency. The framework provides a basis for testing alternative feedback hypotheses against longitudinal data and for optimizing feeding and pumping schedules.

papers.title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
Formation of Electron Velocity Distribution Functions at low-\{beta} Quasi-Perpendicular Shocks From Physical-Mass-Ratio PIC Simulations
papers.abstract: At low-\{beta} quasi-perpendicular shocks, the origins of upstream field-aligned electron beams and downstream flat-top distributions remain unresolved. Using 2D fully kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations at the physical ion-to-electron mass ratio (mi/me = 1836), we found that the shock transition region is dominated by electromagnetic whistler-mode turbulence driven by the modified two-stream instability (MTSI) of reflected ions, not by the electrostatic instabilities as suggested by some previous studies using a reduced mass ratio. Beams in the upstream are produced mainly by shock-drift acceleration (SDA) at the ramp, whereas we attribute the downstream flat-top distributions to nonuniform acceleration by the parallel electric field. Electrons experience different field strengths, polarities, and interaction durations along their trajectories, leading to a spread of parallel velocity changes that broadens and flattens the distribution. These results highlight the importance of using the physical mass ratio in exploring the electron dynamics of low-\{beta} shocks.

papers.title: Exploring Physical Mechanisms Underlying the Emergence of Collective Order
papers.abstract: Emergence of collective order from disordered constituents is a hallmark of active matter, and the Vicsek model (VM) serves as a paradigmatic system for its study. However, whether density-induced emergence in the VM differs between angular (intrinsic) and vectorial (extrinsic) noise, and what mechanisms govern the transitions, remain largely unexplored. Remarkably, we uncover that collective order emerges from a disordered state in a continuous-like manner under intrinsic noise but abruptly under extrinsic noise. Combining nonequilibrium landscape-flux theory with a coarse-grained mapping method, we show that the landscape evolves continuously from a single basin to two and back to one under intrinsic noise, but the two-basin landscape appears abruptly under extrinsic noise across the critical transition to flocking. The counterclockwise nonequilibrium flux sustains global circular motion, providing the driving force for reshaping the landscape. The mean flux and entropy production rate change steeply near the emergence threshold and exhibit pronounced peaks within the coexistence region, identifying them as the dynamical and thermodynamic origins of emergence. Our findings reveal a distinct abrupt emergence under extrinsic noise and offer deeper mechanistic insight, practical applications (e.g., locating phase boundaries and distinguishing transition types), and extensibility to other nonequilibrium collective systems.

papers.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
papers.abstract: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. Exact QMBS states are prepared by applying the inverse isometries to Dicke states. For asymptotic QMBS states, block encoding first prepares the magnon excitations from Dicke states to a prescribed fidelity, after which the inverse isometries map the prepared states back to the physical chains. At fixed target fidelity, the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, implying that a constant number of amplitude amplification rounds suffices. Our algorithm enables systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.

papers.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
papers.abstract: Autoregressive generation over adaptive 3D octrees (Uni-3DAR) offers an intrinsic $O(N \log N)$ sparsity advantage over dense $O(N^2)$ equivariant diffusion and flow models on large drug-like molecules, yet lags in geometric equilibrium, closed-shell valence stability, and property fidelity due to Morton-seam coordinate jumps, leaf-heavy compute with root-count trapping, and target-shortcut collapse in internal critics. We introduce MolGPAO (Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree), a standalone 3D octree architecture and single-output speculative tree-decoding engine using zero external surrogates, zero reinforcement learning, and zero inference-time MLIP relaxation. MolGPAO unifies: (1) non-trapping 6-D ScaleFreeBudgetEmbedding with L5-to-L1 covalent packing priors; (2) a FlashAttention-2 pause-and-gather speculative octree funnel ($m_{s1} \to m_{s2} \to 1$, $M_{\mathrm{out}} = 1$); (3) an anti-shortcut ground-truth TwoStageOctreeProcessCritic with 64-RBF covalent edge gating and $SO(3)$-invariant 12-channel multipole norms (blind QM9 $r = 0.9867$--$0.9989$); (4) a $<0.5$ ms 4-layer $SE(3)$ PostTreeGraphRefiner for Morton-seam healing, expected-XYZ bonded supervision, selective CFG, and zero-heavy-displacement valence reconciliation; and (5) bubble-free stride-2 GPU leaf decoding. Across GEOM-Drugs (0.49 GPU-h), disjoint 50k/50k QM9 (0.43 GPU-h), and PBE0/def2-TZVP-verified OE62 (0.56 GPU-h), MolGPAO lifts drug-scale valid-connected yield 6.78x (12.7% to 86.2%, 99.83% atom stability), runs 7.3x faster (or 1.65x faster at 2.0x yield) than 100-step FlowMol at $N=100$, beats 156 GPU-h PropMolFlow on QM9 HOMO (-12.7%) and dipole (-21.0%) at 362x lower compute, and doubles live DFT hit rate on OE62 (33.3% vs. 16.7%) at 92.8x lower compute.

papers.title: Universal Work Extraction from Individual Sequences by Finite--State Information Engines
papers.abstract: We consider information engines that interact with a heat bath at temperature $T$, a work reservoir, and a tape carrying an individual (deterministic) sequence $x$ over a finite alphabet $\X$. An engine is a cascade of autonomous ratchets with fixed energy levels and detailed--balance dynamics, each processing segments of $m$ tape cells and having finitely many internal states. We prove a converse bound on the extractable work in terms of the empirical block entropies of $x$,and show that it is achievable \emph{universally}, by engines whose energy levels do not depend on $x$. The maximal work per symbol is $kT[\ln|\X|-\bar H(x)]$, where $k$ is Boltzmann's constant and $\bar H(x)$ is the asymptotic normalized aligned block entropy of $x$, which equals its block Lempel--Ziv complexity, and the minimal work needed to erase $x$ is $kT\bar H(x)$ per symbol. Underlying these results is a two--way correspondence with universal coding: energy levels define a code, and a suitably operated cascade extracts $kT$ times $\ln|\X|$ per symbol minus the code length; conversely, a fluctuation identity shows that every engine fixed in advance defines a code. Hence, converses of universal coding apply verbatim to engines; e.g., the optimal redundancy of memoryless universal engines is given by the Shtarkov sum.

papers.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
papers.abstract: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. We also determine multiplicity entropies and correlations between dipole-size sectors. Applying a fixed negative-binomial dipole-to-charged-particle response reproduces the rising trend of the H1 charged-particle multiplicity entropy toward smaller $x$, but does not fully describe the measured multiplicity distributions. These results demonstrate an explicit coherent encoding of finite-state dipole branching and clarify its relation to continuous-cascade fluctuations and DIS phenomenology.

papers.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
papers.abstract: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

papers.title: A predictive scaling framework for hierarchical living systems: From biomacromolecule to the Anthropogenic Earth system
papers.abstract: Living systems, from biomacromolecules to the biosphere, are organized hierarchically with quantitative traits (such as size, mass and lifespan) spanning many orders of magnitude. However, qualitative traits such as structure differ between adjacent levels, and similarities among non-adjacent levels have been recognized only case by case. Yet no framework integrates quantitative and qualitative traits across the hierarchy of living systems. Here, we propose HELIX, a model that couples exponential scaling across levels with trait-based classification. Clustered by 16 traits, the 14 known levels are classified into three groups: Autonomous, Component, and Repeat-autonomous living systems. Levels within each group are self-similar, and the three groups alternate periodically in a helical belt and the quantitative traits follow scaling law. HELIX integrates existing principles from multiple disciplines to form a unified theory. HELIX further predicts three newly emerged levels, illustrating that it can guide cross-level and interdisciplinary research on living systems.

papers.title: Revisiting the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma
papers.abstract: We revisit the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in a quark-gluon plasma with a small momentum-space anisotropy. Within the Braaten-Thoma framework, we obtain the hard contribution in closed form and reduce the soft contribution to one-dimensional integrals. Our result demonstrates analytically that, at linear order in the anisotropy, the dependence on the artificial separation scale cancels between the two contributions. By considering the unnormalized anisotropic distribution together with two variants that hold either the parton number density or the energy density at its isotropic value, we find that the angle-dependent part of the anisotropy correction is identical in all three cases and is proportional to the quadrupole $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is the angle between the heavy-quark velocity and the anisotropy direction. In addition, the sign of the anisotropy correction, which determines whether the energy loss is enhanced or suppressed relative to the isotropic result, depends jointly on the quark speed, coupling, and propagation angle. In particular, at fixed energy density, only the quadrupole term survives. For a positive coefficient of $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, the correction enhances the energy loss for $\cos^2\alpha>1/3$ and suppresses it for $\cos^2\alpha<1/3$, with the opposite behavior for a negative coefficient.

papers.title: The role of hierarchy in Galactic molecular clouds
papers.abstract: To probe the role of hierarchical gas structures in massive star formation, we statistically analyzed 13 Galactic massive star-forming regions using FUGIN CO survey data. Applying a non-binary dendrogram to the position-position-velocity data, we classified the extracted structures into trunks, internal leaves (the densest substructures within trunks), and isolated structures, and compared their properties with an analysis of variance controlling for regional differences. In representative regions, the trunks correspond to morphologies such as filaments and hub-filament systems, or to kinematic signatures of structure-forming events such as cloud-cloud collisions. Across the sample, the trunks are extended, massive, and strongly bound reservoirs, while the leaves are significantly more massive, denser, and more tightly bound than isolated structures of similar spatial scale. Using YSOs and Hi-GAL clumps, we find that the leaves have a lower low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures, whereas their clump formation efficiency is comparable. At a fixed gas mass, the leaves show no higher low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures but convert a larger fraction of their gas into dense clumps. We interpret these contrasts, together with inward gas motions in the position-velocity diagrams, as indicating that the deep potential of the trunks sustains continuous accretion onto the leaves and promotes mutual interactions among them. These processes may raise the characteristic fragmentation mass, as theoretically expected for a dynamically accreting medium, so that a larger fraction of the gas forms massive clumps without a corresponding increase in low-mass star formation. Our single-epoch data constrain only these structural contrasts, but indicate that the gas available for massive star formation is organized on scales larger than a single core.

papers.title: PINN-Slicer: Exploiting Rotational Symmetry to Solve the Photon Orbit Equation Around a Black Hole
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) typically struggle with long-horizon domains, often requiring the network to be retrained as the domain grows. We present PINN-Slicer, a method for second-order autonomous ordinary differential equations, $\ddot{u} = G(u, \dot{u})$, which exploits the invariance of this class of equations under translations of the independent variable. A single PINN, embedded within a solution ansatz that enforces the initial conditions explicitly, is trained on a thin slice of the independent variable using Sobol-sampled initial conditions. The PINN is then deployed recursively, slice-by-slice, across the full domain. We demonstrate PINN-Slicer on the nonlinear equation that describes photon orbits around a black hole, and reach a point-by-point root-mean-square error (RMSE) below $10^{-3}$ in $u = r_s/r$ (the inverse radial coordinate in units of the Schwarzschild radius) relative to a finite-difference reference solution. A key advantage of PINN-Slicer is that a single trained network generalizes to any orbital initial condition within the training range, without retraining. In addition, PINN-Slicer can cope with solution domains that may not be known a priori.

papers.title: Mass Spectral Evidence for Iron Sulfate in Venus' Cloud Aerosol
papers.abstract: Venus' cloud aerosols play pivotal roles in the thermal, chemical, and optical properties of the atmosphere. Here, we present mass spectral evidence that the cloud aerosols contain abundant iron sulfates. Data from the Pioneer Venus Large Probe Neutral Mass Spectrometer (LNMS) suggest that cloud aerosols inadvertently collected into the inlets at ~48-51 km and thermally decomposed below the clouds, releasing several compounds into the LNMS. At 23 km and below, multiple iron species (54Fe+, 56FeO+, 54FeO+, 56Fe2O+, and 56Fe2O2+) and other decomposition gases were detected. Quantitative treatment of these mass signals suggested the release of Fe2O3, SO2, O2, SO3, H2SO4, and H2O, consistent with the thermal decomposition of hydronium-bearing ferric sulfates. The resulting mole ratio for iron to sulfate (2.0 +/- 1.1) aligns with hydronium jarosite ((H3O)Fe3(SO4)2(OH)6), which likely formed within the inlets after aerosol capture, dehydration, and loss of sulfuric acid. Our thermochemical calculations support these assessments. Speciation of the ferric sulfates in the native aerosols remains unconstrained (e.g., solution and/or particle phases). Peak fits to the thermal release profiles yielded the abundances of the bulk iron (0.8 +/- 0.4 mg m-3) and aerosol-derived compounds, including hydronium jarosite (2.2 +/- 1.2 mg m-3, 30 +/- 17 wt%), water (3.7 +/- 0.4 mg m-3, 50 +/- 10 wt%), and sulfuric acid (1.5 +/- 0.2 mg m-3, 20 +/- 5 wt%). Surface sourcing of the cloud iron is likely minor. Instead, cosmic dust influx could deliver iron to the clouds in a geologically short time (2.4 +/- 1.5 Myr).

papers.title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
papers.abstract: In the two-dimensional (2D) Gross-Pitaevskii model for a Bose gas, the naive dimensional non-equilibrium wave-turbulence power-law prediction for the direct energy cascade coincides with thermal equilibrium and therefore carries no energy flux. We resolve this degeneracy by deriving a logarithmically corrected spectrum that supports a positive, constant energy flux toward small scales. A systematic asymptotic expansion of the wave-kinetic collision integral determines the logarithmic exponent to be 1/3, while the small-scale dissipation scale sets the upper cutoff in the logarithmic correction. Regularization of a marginal infrared divergence at the forcing scale yields an estimate of the spectral prefactor for asymptotically well-separated forcing and dissipation scales. Simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic equations support the predicted spectral shape. Over finite spectral ranges, the correction produces apparent power laws steeper than the dimensional prediction, offering a possible explanation for the steep spectra observed in 2D Bose gas experiments. Our approach provides a systematic framework for constructing wave turbulent cascade spectra when the power-law prediction is degenerate with thermodynamic equilibrium.

papers.title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
papers.abstract: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $\Delta v_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

papers.title: Transport Layer-Driven Optimization of Color and Efficiency in TADF OLEDs for Large-Area Applications
papers.abstract: Balancing structural simplicity with high efficiency is crucial for practical applications of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), especially in large-area lighting devices. Optimizing the charge-transport layers in multilayer OLEDs controls the recombination zone within the emissive layer, thereby enhancing the device's performance. Herein, we experimentally and computationally investigate how the thicknesses of the electron and hole transport layers affect the performance of orange-red thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) OLEDs. Using a TADF emitter, 2-[4-(diphenylamino)phenyl]-10,10-dioxide-9H-thioxanthen-9-one (TXO-TPA), at 10 wt\% concentration in 4,4-Bis(N-carbazolyl)-1,1-biphenyl (CBP) host, we achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency ($\eta_{EQE}$) of 20.86\% and a peak luminance of 32,800 cd m$^{-2}$. Using a combination of drift-diffusion and optical simulations, we reveal how variations in hole- and electron-transport-layer thicknesses modulate the charge-carrier balance and shift the recombination zone within the emissive layer. This tuning not only optimizes exciton formation but also enables color tuning from green to red without altering the emissive material. Our findings highlight the critical role of transport layer engineering in achieving efficient, color-controlled OLEDs with simplified architectures. Furthermore, we successfully demonstrate a large-area OLED device (~20 cm$^{2}$), achieving an impressive $\eta_{EQE}$ of 17\%, underscoring the scalability and practicality of our approach for general lighting applications.

papers.title: Almost sure lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of critical AMO
papers.abstract: We show that there exists an absolute constant $d>0$ such that for almost all frequencies $\alpha\in[0,1]\setminus\Q$, the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of the critical almost Mathieu operator $H_{1,\alpha,\theta}$ is bounded from below by $d$.

papers.title: Revisiting the Schottky-Mott Relation for Metal/ Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Interfaces: The Role of Interface Dipoles
papers.abstract: High contact resistance, predominantly stemming from Fermi-level pinning (FLP), becomes a critical bottleneck in the contact engineering of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) based two-dimensional field-effect transistors (2DFETs). Our study re-examines the inherent nature of FLP in 2D semiconductors, particularly focusing on regimes where the material thickness is commensurate with the interface thickness. Through the synergistic application of first-principles calculations and experimental validation via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), we rigorously establish the metal effective work function (eWF) as the definitive figure of merit for substantiating the Schottky-Mott relation. Our findings indicate that FLP is intrinsically governed by both long-range dipole interactions and extended short-range Lennard-Jones potentials. This framework, in conjunction with the linear Schottky-Mott relation, improves predictive capabilities in contact engineering.

papers.title: Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Reconstruction of Discrete space Population Dynamics
papers.abstract: Reconstructing the continuous time dynamics of cell state evolution from sparse snapshot observations can be formulated as an unbalanced optimal transport problem. To study such dynamics at a coarse grained cell type level, unbalanced optimal transport must be extended to discrete state spaces. Inspired by discrete flow matching, we extended the dynamic Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) problem to discrete spaces, and derived a closed form for its solution. For particularly large state spaces or more general models, we proposed an unbalanced discrete flow matching as a numerical approximation method, which provides a Markovian reconstruction of the optimal WFR flow. Our discrete WFR framework also stays stable across different coarse grain resolution. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach, and applications to real biological data supported the plausibility of the reconstructed dynamics.

papers.title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

papers.title: Phono3GPU: GPU-Accelerated Linear Tetrahedron Integration for Phonon Thermal Transport
papers.abstract: Materials with high or low thermal conductivity are increasingly important for thermal management and energy technologies. Machine-learned interatomic potentials have accelerated anharmonic force-constant calculations, shifting the bottleneck toward phonon transport calculations for large materials datasets. Existing GPU solvers often rely on smearing, whose width can require material-dependent choices, while the linear tetrahedron method used in phono3py avoids this parameter but becomes costly for complex structures. Here we introduce Phono3GPU, which reformulates three-phonon scattering and linear tetrahedron integration for massively parallel GPU execution. Across benchmark crystals, Phono3GPU accelerates total calculations by up to 41 times relative to a CPU implementation, with larger gains for complex unit cells, and by 2 to 6 times relative to a recent GPU plug-in for phono3py. We further demonstrate atom-resolved scattering analysis in defective silicon supercells as an application enabled by the reduced computational cost. Phono3GPU thus lowers the cost of tetrahedron-based thermal-conductivity calculations and of detailed investigations of structure-dependent phonon transport.

papers.title: Fast radio bursts track cosmic star formation history with time delay: the effect of burst fluence
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are luminous millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin, yet their progenitor systems remain unidentified. The redshift evolution of the FRB event rate provides a powerful, model-independent discriminant between young progenitors and old progenitors, but recent studies have reached conflicting conclusions. In this work, we perform a forward-modeling analysis of the apparent non-repeating FRB sample from the CHIME/FRB catalogs to constrain the intrinsic FRB population. We find that the FRB rate follows the star formation rate (SFR) with little time delay when both dispersion measure (DM) and fluence are considered. In contrast, when only DM is taken into account, a significant time delay ($3 \sim 4$ Gyr) exists between the FRB rate and the SFR. The main reason for this discrepancy is that systematic biases exist in the mapping process from burst fluence to signal-to-noise ratio. These results support that at least a fraction of FRBs arise from a progenitor population whose event rate is delayed relative to star formation.

papers.title: Directional Statistics of Synchrotron Polarization in Mixed Emitting and Faraday-Rotating Turbulence
papers.abstract: Polarization directions provide a sensitive probe of Faraday rotation without weighting the signal by polarized brightness. We develop their spatial statistics for a turbulent volume in which synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation coexist. For independent, zero-mean Gaussian polarized emissivity, we derive an exact relation for the directional correlation. We derive strong stochastic coherence-depth scalings, including an additional interval for steep Faraday-density spectra, and distinguish them from the conditions needed to infer directional spectral slopes. We also quantify the weak-rotation response of a coherent uniform emitter and demonstrate that the scalings of the normalized tangential polarization gradient follow directly from the direction spectrum. A combined use of the techniques, including those introduced earlier in Lazarian & Pogosyan (2016), provides a way for detailed study of astrophysical turbulence.

papers.title: Cascading LO-phonon-mediated resonant energy transfer from excitons to Eu3+ for ultrahigh color purity red luminescence in europium-doped GaN
papers.abstract: High-efficiency, wavelength-stable red micro-LEDs with ultrahigh color purity remain a critical bottleneck for monolithic III-nitride full-color displays. Europium-doped GaN (GaN:Eu) offers a compelling solution, yet the microscopic energy transfer mechanism from the GaN host to Eu3+ ions has remained unresolved for three decades, impeding rational performance optimization. Here we report polaron-mediated resonant energy transfer in high-crystalline-quality GaN:Eu epilayers grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Eu3+ doping stabilizes a distinct bound exciton (BX3) state at 3.478 eV, which couples strongly with longitudinal optical (LO) phonons via the Frohlich interaction to form cascading polarons with up to seven phonon replicas at a uniform energy spacing of 92.0+/-0.7 meV. The BX3 polaron coupled with 5LO phonons matches precisely the 7F0-->5D3 intra-4f transition energy of Eu3+ at 3.019 eV. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence reveals non-equilibrium phonon emission, evidencing directional resonant energy transfer. After rapid nonradiative relaxation from the 5D3 excited state to the 5D0 metastable state, the hypersensitive 5D0-->7F2 transition yields sharp 622 nm red emission. Time-resolved spectroscopy confirms a single dominant Eu3+ luminescent site with reduced local symmetry, attributed to off-axis EuGa-VN complexes. This work identifies a key energy transfer channel and provides a clear framework for designing high-efficiency GaN:Eu red emitter.

papers.title: Structural Anisotropy in Bi$_2$Se$_3$/$λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ Topological Insulator/Superconductor Bilayer
papers.abstract: We investigate the crystallographic-orientation dependence of the response of $\lambda$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ ($\lambda$-Ga) to Bi$_2$Se$_3$ deposition. Cross-sectional focused-ion-beam (FIB) imaging confirms formation of a deposited Bi$_2$Se$_3$-containing layer and a distinct interface with $\lambda$-Ga. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD) shows that the coated $\lambda$-Ga crystal remains structurally intact but exhibits a strongly orientation-dependent, non-monotonic response, with the largest modification for the $ab$-plane after 4 min of deposition, whereas the $ac$-plane remains comparatively unchanged. This condition corresponds to the intermediate-deposition regime previously identified at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ thickness of approximately 110 nm. First-principles calculations based on the refined structures show the largest orientation-dependent electronic modification under the same conditions. Complementary optical spectroscopy of Bi$_2$Se$_3$/SiO$_2$ films shows deposition-time-dependent evolution of the film response. These results establish a pronounced crystallographic anisotropy in the structural and calculated electronic response of $\lambda$-Ga to Bi$_2$Se$_3$ deposition.

papers.title: Self-Assembled Triangular Sc-rich Nanodomains: The Orign of Anomalous Alloy Scattering in ScAlN/GaN Heterostructures
papers.abstract: Wurtzite scandium aluminium nitride (ScAlN) alloys hold substantial potential for GaN heterostructure high-electron mobility transistors, owing to their large spontaneous polarization gradient and the ability to achieve precise lattice matching at heterointerface. Nevertheless, despite continuous advances in epitaxy and device fabrication, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) mobility in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures remains persistently limited, and the underlying microscopic origin remains elusive. Here, we uncover an anomalous electron scattering mechanism from laterally correlated alloy disorder that spontaneously develops within the ScAlN barrier driven by strain-field undulations imposed by threading dislocations. Dislocation strain field partitions the growth front into nanoscale domains with distinct strain states, driving anisotropic diffusion of Sc adatoms and yielding crystallographically oriented triangular Sc-rich nanodomains. Reducing the threading dislocation density from 2.8E10 to 4.4E8 cm^-2 suppresses areal density of nanodomains by more than two orders of magnitude. As a result, low-temperature Hall mobility increases from 1800 to 11995 cm^2*V^-1*s^-1. These findings establish dislocation-mediated Sc-rich nanodomains as the dominant source of anomalously strong alloy scattering, resolving the mobility bottleneck for high-performance nitride electronics.

papers.title: Cosmographic Analysis of Gravitational Baryogenesis in Running-$G$ Cosmology
Origin of flavour cancellations in thermal leptogenesis
papers.abstract: In thermal leptogenesis with three hierarchical heavy neutrinos $N_1$, $N_2$ and $N_3$, the baryon asymmetry can be the small remainder of large contributions that cancel. Interference terms in the CP asymmetry are known to contribute to the final asymmetry through flavour-dependent washout. However, it remains unclear where the cancellation occurs, how large the interference contribution is, and how the accuracy of approximate equations changes when this information is lost. We split the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them with Standard Model transport equations. We find that the cancellation occurs mainly between the diagonal and off-diagonal parts of the same heavy neutrino, and that it is caused by flavour-dependent washout. We also find that the interference between the lepton state produced in the decay and the states orthogonal to it typically accounts for most of the $N_2$ and $N_3$ contribution. Approximations that reduce the CP asymmetry to flavour populations turn out to miss most of this contribution, whereas density-matrix equations with the full CP-asymmetry matrix agree much better.

papers.title: Constraining the Inner Accretion Geometry of GX 9+9 with Broadband Spectral and Timing Studies
papers.abstract: We present a broadband spectral and timing study of the bright atoll neutron star low-mass X-ray binary GX~9+9, using simultaneous NICER, NuSTAR, and MAXI observations from 2019 and 2022. The broadband spectra are well described by a combination of multicolor disk emission, thermal Comptonization of blackbody seed photons from the neutron star surface or boundary layer, and associated disk reflection. We report a clear detection of reflection features in this source, including a moderately broad Fe K$\alpha$ complex and a reflection hump, confirming an earlier detection from a different observation. These features likely arise from the illumination of the moderately ionized disk by thermally Comptonized emission from the boundary layer or warm corona. While the source remained in the soft spectral state during both observations, the 2022 observation exhibits a relatively larger thermal contribution, together with a steeper Comptonized component and lower coronal optical depth. Both reflection and disk-continuum modeling favor a truncated disk, with the latter indicating a smaller inner disk radius in 2022. The inferred radial extent of the boundary layer of $\sim8~r_{\rm g}$ may play a role in the observed disk truncation. Assuming that the disk is truncated at the magnetospheric radius, we obtain an upper limit on the magnetic field strength of $\lesssim3\times10^{10}$ G. Timing analysis reveals a relatively stable disk component and a highly variable Comptonized component, consistent with the typical characteristics of the soft state.

papers.title: On a new resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group E(2)
papers.abstract: We provide a non-divergent resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group $E(2)$, replacing the integral on the whole group with the Haar measure by an invariant integration with non local kernels constructed by Steinberg and Wolf in 1981, valid for solutions of Helmholtz equation, that appears in natural way as the eigenvalue equation of the Casimir operator of $E(2)$. With this construction, all properties of Perelomov coherent states are preserved, in particular covariance, and all square-integrable functions are addmissible, improving previous results like those of de Bièvre and Torrésani.

papers.title: Geometry Sets the Neutral MLIP-DFT Gap in Non-Covalent Binding, and Charged Systems Fail
papers.abstract: Pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are widely expected to substitute for explicit quantum chemistry when screening molecular interactions. On non-covalent binding we find that this expectation holds for neutral chemistry and fails for charged chemistry. We audit the FAIRChem UMA OMol head, without task-specific fine-tuning, on 5,567 probe-target dimers from 18 benchmarks across nine fidelity arms, using RAPIDS (Rapid Atomistic Probe-target Interaction Discovery Scaffold), a training-free inference-time scaffold. First, on neutral chemistry RAPIDS reaches a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.37 kcal/mol, matching or beating every explicit DFT single-point fidelity (1.42-1.50 kcal/mol), so the remaining MLIP-DFT gap is geometric rather than a learned-surface error. Second, charged systems form a qualitatively different regime: MAE jumps to 8.5-22.9 kcal/mol across three charged benchmarks; DFT single-point rescoring does not restore accuracy, geometry reoptimization restores it for ionic hydrogen bonds and ion-molecule dimers, and the failure persists across all three MLIP backbones. Third, the residual failures are structured: signed biases cluster by chemistry family, and whether a fidelity fails catastrophically transfers across families more reliably than error magnitude, enabling cost-aware fidelity selection. RAPIDS-Select, a closed-form rule on cheap precomputed features, uses about 37% less compute than a strong static DFT baseline at matched accuracy, and on a newly computed charged benchmark cuts the catastrophe rate from 68% to 5.7%. On WetSenseBench, a wet-lab-grounded host-guest selectivity benchmark from eight sensing studies, RAPIDS without DFT follow-up recovers 82.9% pair-level agreement on the seven studies above its ~1 kcal/mol precision floor.

papers.title: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence
papers.abstract: Self-interacting neutrino gases exhibit collective behavior, in which additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability. We investigate the effects of energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity on the resulting flavor conversion through linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations. We find contrasting wavenumber dependences for the near/gapless and far/gapped branches, with maximum growth rates at collision-scale shifted wavenumbers and at collective-scale wavenumbers, respectively. Their eigenvectors reveal distinct energy and angular structures, which are reflected in the subsequent establishment of flavor swap and equipartition. The nonlinear evolution also features secondary flavor growth associated with changes in the stability of collective modes as the neutrino background evolves. Despite the spreading of flavor coherence across spatial scales due to nonlinear mode coupling, collisional decoherence tends to limit the development of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous. These findings represent a step towards understanding and predicting the nonlinear flavor evolution of dense neutrino gases interacting with their surroundings, particularly in explosive astrophysical environments.

papers.title: Spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
papers.abstract: Strong spin-orbit coupling in $5d$ ions produces multipolar orders that conventional probes barely detect. In cubic $5d^1$ double perovskites, the spin-orbit quartet couples to Jahn-Teller vibrations, and resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) has established the resulting spin-orbit-lattice entangled (vibronic) states [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{133}, 036501 (2024)]. We proposed that these vibronic states order cooperatively and thereby explain the hidden quadrupole and canted magnetic phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ [Phys. Rev. B \textbf{107}, L220404 (2023)], but that proposal rested on a simplified model. Here, we show that a spin-vibronic Hamiltonian derived from first principles, with a single scale factor for the elastic coupling, reproduces the ordered phases of Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ with the same vibronic states that describe its RIXS spectra. With this factor bringing the quadrupolar transition to 34.7 K, near the measured 33 K, the theory predicts the magnetic transition at 19.3 K, against the measured 18 K, and reproduces the antiferro distortion and the ferro elongation between the transitions. These results support spin-vibronic order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and point to it as the origin of the hidden multipolar phases of $5d^1$ double perovskites.

papers.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
papers.abstract: RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences that fold into specified target structures. Existing methods rely on learned generators that can miss exact structural matches, especially beyond their training distributions, or on costly search over a vast, multimodal sequence space. Search is further complicated by globally coupled nucleotide interactions, as correcting one pairing error can create new errors beyond a fixed repair scope. To address this, we introduce KnitNet, an inference-time scaling framework that learns from verifier feedback to refine sequences for exact fold-back matching. Starting from candidates generated for a target secondary structure, KnitNet uses mismatched folds to infer nucleotide dependencies and adapt its joint repair strategy, while an online surrogate learns to predict which edits are promising. This makes search progressively more informed and compute-efficient. Crucially, KnitNet generalizes across RNA structural regimes by changing only the optimization signal to match the verifier required by each setting. Across five secondary-structure benchmarks, KnitNet increases exact solve rates by an average of 21 percentage points over continued sampling with 70% less time-to-solve. On OpenKnot57 specifically, KnitNet is the first method to achieve exact computational matches for all complex, pseudoknotted structures. Beyond 2D, KnitNet improves 3D structural self-consistency over per-target RL by 7.8% while being 39.3% faster, demonstrating generalization and effective inference-time scaling across RNA design regimes.

papers.title: Controlling truncation errors in loop tensor network renormalization
papers.abstract: At finite bond dimension $\chi$, tensor network renormalization (TNR) of a critical model eventually becomes gapped. For LoopTNR with $O(2)$ symmetry on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, parametrized by the Luttinger parameter $K$, we show that the correlation length $\xi$ of the gapped phase is set by the seed of the dimerization injected by the truncation, and depends on $\chi$ only through it. Read from a weak-coupling window early in the same run, the seed predicts $\xi=10^3$-$10^{16}$ via the sine-Gordon mass-coupling relation with no free parameter, to within a few percent for $K\le1.5$ and about 10% at $K=1.75$; since the seed fluctuates strongly with $\chi$, $\xi$ is not monotonic in $\chi$. An alternation of the vertex weights shifts the seed; with its sign read from a $\pi$ twist, one short calibration predicts a counterterm that delays the breakdown in 16 of the 17 compensated groups of a campaign fixed in advance. A correction of the coarse-grained tensors, repeated during the flow, keeps the runs at $K=1$ and $1.5$ critical up to step 160, the last step computed, and exposes the marginal truncation error that remains. Our findings illustrate a systematic procedure for controlling the relevant truncation error, and thereby extending the critical window, in tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension.

papers.title: Superconductivity from a Cooper surface instability in a nodal Bose metal
papers.abstract: In underdoped cuprates, the superconducting gap is largest where low-energy electron spectral weight is already depleted above the transition. How can a weak attraction drive superconductivity when the one-electron density of states vanishes? In a momentum-space \(t\)--\(J\) model, the exactly solvable normal state is a nodal Bose metal with four one-electron nodes.
