The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $\chi$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $\chi$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.

papers.title: Mutual Linearity in Nonlinear Population Dynamics
papers.abstract: Mutual linearity, the persistence of affine relations among stationary observables under arbitrarily strong changes of one transition rate, is known for Markov jump processes and chemical reaction networks. We show that generalized Lotka--Volterra dynamics form a new class of mutually linear systems, even though species can go extinct and attractors can be chaotic. Any change to one species' equation acts on the others as one effective press and keeps all abundances affinely related: piecewise across extinctions, and as time averages on chaotic attractors.

papers.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--Păun, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of indoor disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, in the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS)[13], which combines architectural layout, people movement and airborne viral transmission, aerosol concentrations are assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation. Also, particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we extend VIRIS to the VIRIS-3D-L framework to investigate how these two assumptions affect the predicted infection risk. In VIRIS-3D-L, we solve the reaction-diffusion equation in three dimensions (3D), and aerosol deposition is represented by local surface removal through a Robin boundary condition. We compare VIRIS with VIRIS-3D-L across three indoor settings of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home, and a supermarket. For the courtroom, care home, and supermarket, respectively, at the end of the simulation, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts average infection risks across individuals of 44%, 78%, and 25%, while VIRIS-3D-L predicts risks of 51%, 85%, and 28%. Thus, VIRIS significantly underestimates infection risk in all three settings. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show agreement with a documented courtroom outbreak that was used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between eight minutes and just under 1.5 hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk in indoor spaces without prohibitive computational costs.

papers.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

papers.title: Optimizing one-dimensional lithographically defined nanowires in semiconducting heterostructures
papers.abstract: One-dimensional nanowires can host remarkable electronic properties and are central to studying quantum transport. Although heterostructure-defined confinement combined with gate-defined potentials can greatly reduce the effects of impurities as measured via electron mobilities, the realization and interpretation of novel effects at this scale are complicated by disorder. Experiments on lithographically defined one-dimensional nanowires therefore do not exhibit ideal behavior. Using theoretical and computational models, we predict that optimizing the geometry of split gates in semiconducting heterostructures will lead to higher-quality channels for transport measurements. Further, we show that this optimization is essential for resolving features of interest such as the Rashba-induced spin gap. This new approach to lithographically defined conduction channels provides better energy resolution and is less susceptible to disorder.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count---the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $\bd{G(i\epsilon)}$---and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Luttinger's theorem seemingly follows from particle-number conservation alone, without resorting to perturbation theory, and yet it is found to be violated. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is a pure zero-frequency boundary term, which the conventional proof implicitly discards. Hence, violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton-diagram formalism, whose validity is independent of the convergence of the skeleton-diagram expansion to the exact solution. This advancement in understanding resolves a longstanding point of contention in many-body theory. We also find that the Luttinger integral is a genuine topological invariant, tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional rather than to the Green's function alone; like the monodromy of $\bd{\ln G(i\epsilon)}$, it stems exclusively from the zero-frequency point where the Matsubara trajectory crosses the branch cut of the logarithm. Correspondingly, the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger integral makes the Hall number in topological insulators differ from its Green's-function expression by a vertex correction, itself invariant, which can take fractional values.

papers.title: Hidden Triakontadipole Order in the Triangular-Lattice Magnet CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$
papers.abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom, and establish a dipole--triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K via precision tensor-network calculations. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus offer a hidden-order caveat for spin-liquid searches and provide a new platform for exploring high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM Research Agents as Tests of Return Predictability
papers.abstract: How often do research agents built on large language models report that they can forecast returns when the data contain no signal? We score the conclusions of four such agents as statistical decisions on the same simulated monthly return series. Without a prescribed significance level, the agents reported that their forecasts would beat the expanding historical mean in 16-44% of 110 null samples, whereas a Holm-adjusted regression test rejected the absence of predictability in 8% of the same samples. When a weak predictor was present, comparisons at matched false-positive rates did not establish a detection advantage for the three commercial agents. Instructing those agents to report outperformance only if they would reject the absence of predictability at the 5% level, accounting for every specification they evaluated, reduced their false-positive rates to 0-3%. It also reduced detection at a population $R^2$ of 1%: from 74% to 45% for Claude Opus 5.5, from 59% to 6% for GPT-6.1 Sol and from 71% to 15% for GPT-6.1 Terra. Whether the instruction holds the false-positive rate at 5% remains unresolved. For researchers who delegate the search for return predictors to an agent, specifying the final comparison deserves as much attention as choosing the forecasting model.

papers.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
papers.abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.

papers.title: The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation
papers.abstract: We prove that every orbitally stable soliton of the pure-power generalized Benjamin--Bona--Mahony (gBBM) equation is locally asymptotically stable. For both nonlinearities $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u$ and $f(u)=|u|^p$, the result holds for every exponent $p>1$ throughout the orbital stability range $c>c^*(p)$. Solutions starting sufficiently close to one of these solitons in the energy space converge locally in a moving frame to a nearby soliton and the limiting soliton has a speed close to that of the initial soliton. This establishes, for pure-power gBBM, the local convergence predicted by Bona and Soyeur's asymptotic stability conjecture and addresses an open problem raised by Martel. The proof uses Kato smoothing to close the high-energy virial estimates. The required smoothing estimates rely on the absence of nonzero embedded eigenvalues of the linearized operator. We establish this spectral property for every $p>1$ and every soliton speed $c>1$, including speeds for which the soliton is orbitally unstable. This settles a Pego--Weinstein spectral conjecture in the pure-power gBBM case.

papers.title: Renormalization for Robust Memory without Synchronization
papers.abstract: Local error correction can preserve classical information against noise, but protection under synchronized updates need not survive when sites evolve at independent random times. Establishing stability is particularly challenging when protection relies on the collective action of competing local rules. Here we develop a spacetime renormalization framework that reveals how independently acting local updates can collectively stabilize memory. We identify sufficient conditions under which the geometry of stable interfaces and suppression of defect propagation produce reliable erosion at large scales. Applying this framework, we prove the stability of the asynchronous R squeezing code and introduce robust processes in two and three dimensions. In these systems, both encoded phases persist under sufficiently weak noise, even when the noise favors one phase. Our results provide a criterion for designing autonomous memories sustained by competing local stochastic dynamics.

papers.title: Integral permutation twisted cohomology: one auspicious twist is all you need
papers.abstract: We introduce a reduced form of permutation twisted cohomology for the derived category of permutation modules over any commutative ring. Unlike the twisted cohomology rings previously constructed by Balmer--Gallauer and Miller, this reduced twisted cohomology ring is only bigraded, twisted by a single, well-chosen endotrivial complex corresponding to the representation sphere arising from the (doubled) regular real representation of a group. We prove that over any commutative ring, the Balmer spectrum of the derived category of permutation modules is homeomorphic to the projectivization of the spectrum of the reduced twisted cohomology ring. Moreover, we show that if the base ring is Noetherian, this ring is finite over the finitely generated subalgebra generated by the forerunners, certain $p$-local isomorphisms, of the twist. We apply these results to further analyze the geometry of permutation modules, determine the local Picard group of the geometric open of the Balmer spectrum, and resolve other questions posed by Miller. We include an appendix giving a general criterion for finite generation of twisted cohomology rings in tensor-triangular geometry.

papers.title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
papers.abstract: We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $\Phi_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|\lambda|$, we construct pure ground states $\omega_{\lambda}$ of the interacting bulk system $\Phi_{\lambda}=\Phi_h+\lambda\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $\beta_{0,\lambda}$ such that $\omega_{\lambda}=\omega_0\circ\beta_{0,\lambda}$, where $\omega_0$ is the free ground state of $\Phi_h$. Each $\omega_\lambda$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|\lambda| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm. Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator. The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.

papers.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

papers.title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
papers.abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.

papers.title: Revealing irregularities through distributional discrepancies in latent space via Stein-witness estimation
papers.abstract: RIDDLE is a new method for resonant anomaly detection that uses a scalar Stein-witness function to identify discrepancies between unlabeled signal-region events and a background distribution inferred from dijet-mass sidebands. The witness is optimized in a latent representation of auxiliary jet observables against a differentiable background reference, without requiring an explicit signal model. The method is evaluated using simulated LHC Olympics dijet events and compared with its idealized and supervised benchmarks, which share the same statistical construction but use additional background or signal information, and with LaCATHODE as an independent anomaly detection method. RIDDLE demonstrates strong signal-background discrimination comparable to the idealized benchmark, generally outperforming LaCATHODE while largely preserving the background dijet-mass spectrum under anomaly-score selection. Tests incorporating additional angular information and deliberately mass-correlated features further demonstrate the method's robustness under the studied conditions. Together, these results highlight the potential of RIDDLE as a robust, data-driven approach for enhanced resonance searches that combines effective anomaly discrimination with background-shape preservation.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
papers.abstract: We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. Tóth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since Tóth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. Tóth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.

papers.title: In Situ Thermal Preparation by CO2-Laser and Chemical Characterization of Oxide Substrates Across Multiple Crystallographic Orientations
papers.abstract: Atomically flat and chemically controlled oxide substrate surfaces are essential for high-quality epitaxial growth of complex materials and heterostructures. Previous studies have demonstrated in situ thermal preparation of selected oxide substrates, primarily focusing on conventional low-index orientations such as SrTiO$_3$ (100) and LaAlO$_3$ (100). Here, we extend these methodologies to a broader range of oxide substrates and crystallographic orientations, including challenging polar surfaces. We present a systematic study of the in situ thermal preparation of SrTiO$_3$ (100), SrTiO$_3$ (111), GdScO$_3$ (110), LaAlO$_3$ (111), (LaAlO$_3$)$_{0.3}$(Sr$_2$AlTaO$_6$)$_{0.7}$ (001), and NdGaO$_3$ (110) single crystal substrates. The substrates are annealed in a vacuum chamber under a controlled oxygen background environment using a CO$_2$ laser heating system. The optimized annealing conditions produce atomically flat step-and-terrace structures, long-range surface crystallinity, and effectively clean surfaces across all the investigated substrates. Our results establish a versatile, reproducible, and broadly applicable platform for the in situ preparation of oxide substrates immediately prior to epitaxial growth. These results also provide practical guidelines for interface engineering and surface-sensitive investigations of complex materials.

papers.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
Wrapping M5-branes on a non-spin manifold: Spin$^h$ structures and AdS$_7$ black holes
papers.abstract: We construct a solution of seven-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_5$, where $M_5$ is the five-dimensional Wu manifold $SU(3)/SO(3)$. The solution is supersymmetric, despite the fact that the Wu manifold admits neither a spin structure nor a spin$^c$ structure. Rather, it admits a spin$^h$ structure, wherein the ill-definedness of ordinary spinors due to a minus sign in their holonomy is compensated by a further minus sign arising through the spinors carrying $SO(3)$ Yang-Mills charge, in a half-integer isospin representation of the $SU(2)$ double cover of the $SO(3)$. We show how the configuration can be lifted to a solution of $D=11$ supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_9$, where $M_9$ is the unit tangent bundle of the Wu manifold. We discuss the geometry and topology of $M_9$, and study the supersymmetry from the eleven-dimensional standpoint. We extend the seven-dimensional solution to a black hole, and discuss some aspects of its holographic interpretation and the UV to IR flow. We revisit a previously-known AdS$_2\times H^3\times H^2$ solution, and its UV to IR flow, showing that the flow equations in fact admit of an exact solution. Additionally, we give a detailed discussion of the lift of the AdS$_2\times S^5$ solution to $D=11$, exhibiting similarities and differences between the properties of its internal space $M_9$ (the unit tangent bundle of $S^5$) and the Wu manifold example of our main discussion. We also construct the non-compact dual of the Wu manifold solution, where $M_5$ is taken to be $SL(3,\mathbb R)/SO(3)$.

papers.title: Regular Additive Scalar Invariants of ${\mathcal N}=1$ Hyperbolic Spin Supertriangles
papers.abstract: We classify regular cyclic scalar invariants of non-degenerate hyperbolic ${\mathcal N}=1$ spin supertriangles which are additive under geodesic subdivision. After fixing the spin lift, the common-first gauge (introduced in earlier work by the second-named author and further developed here) gives a complete $3|4$ modulus of such supertriangles.. The space of additive scalar invariants is proved to have superdimension $3|1$: ordinary hyperbolic area in degree zero, two even generators in degree two, and one odd generator in degree three; the degree-one and degree-four sectors vanish. One degree-two generator is the fermionic first variation of body area, equivalently the nilpotent correction from ordinary body angle defect to super angle defect. The degree-three generator changes sign under reversal of the spin lift, while the other generators are fixed, so ordinary supertriangles carry only three even invariants.

papers.title: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
Orientation-Dependent Universality of Spin-Conductance Fluctuations in d-Wave Altermagnets
papers.abstract: Universal conductance fluctuations reflect the symmetry and geometry of phase-coherent transport. However, it remains unclear whether crystal orientation relative to the device can tune fluctuation plateaus in spin-conserving altermagnets. Here, using quantum transport simulations of a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with scalar disorder, we show that crystal orientation tunes longitudinal and spin-Hall fluctuation plateaus while each spin sector remains in the orthogonal symmetry class. At intermediate disorder, tuning the crystal orientation toward the device diagonal weakens longitudinal spin-conductance fluctuations and enhances spin-Hall fluctuations. Both responses exhibit well-defined plateaus at the diagonal orientation, with amplitudes that depend only weakly on disorder and altermagnetic strength over the ranges studied. A variance decomposition shows that, at this orientation, increasing disorder drives the longitudinal spin-channel covariance toward zero, while the transverse covariance shifts from enhancing to suppressing the spin-Hall variance. Our findings suggest that spin-conductance fluctuations can probe transport anisotropy in altermagnets.

papers.title: The Generalized BEADS Representation: A Correlation-Based Visualization of Mixed Quantum States
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics and particularly quantum information theory suffer from a lack of intuitive images. Visualization tools offer novel perspectives on many problems in quantum physics by revealing important properties of quantum states and processes that are otherwise obscured by abstract mathematical formalisms. Here, we extend the previously established BEADS representation of pure states to the so-called generalized BEADS representation of mixed quantum states. We introduce spherical functions, so-called beads to visualize correlation structures of mixed quantum states in an informationally complete way. A recursive optimization scheme is used to obtain minimum-entanglement pure state decompositions of all subsystems of a given N-qubit state. We show how correlation function components can be decomposed into individual contributions that correspond to different types of correlations of mixed states. This allows us to visually characterize the total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, nonclassical quantum-discord-type correlations as well as classical correlations. We further introduce a new quantifier for W-type entanglement for identifying W-class states. After outlining the mathematical details relevant for constructing the representation, we examine the generalized BEADS representations for various types of mixed states including product, classically correlated, separable but nonclassically correlated, as well as entangled states. As exemplary applications of the generalized BEADS representation, we showcase entanglement distillation and the effects of noise channels.

papers.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
papers.abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest. We also show that, in an arbitrary semi-abelian category, an extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ is central relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of two-nilpotent objects, defined by means of the ternary Higgins commutator, precisely when the ternary Higgins commutator $[K,A,A]_{\mathsf{Hig}}$ vanishes; a similar characterization holds in the $n$-nilpotent case.

papers.title: Quantum limit cycles from phase coupling: A framework for NISQ thermodynamic devices
papers.abstract: Quantum decoherence does not permit the operation of (new) miniaturised devices or protocols that can otherwise run unassisted in classical settings, without explicit user agent intervention in the quantum realm. Classical driving signals are inadequate to model a truly quantum device built entirely in the quantum realm. Synchronisation endures miniaturisation without sacrificing quantum coherence, unlike thermalisation. We quantise the Kuramoto model and the Van der Pol oscillator and couple it with qubit(s) to show a robust limit cycle even in typical quantum thermodynamical settings. Novel effects such as Entanglement State Revivals, Zeno locking and thermal current interference are observed. We propose toy model devices that can be implemented harnessing the Synchronisation of a qubit (or an arbitrary collection of qubits) with a nonlinear phase oscillator. The framework theory used here, Spectral Mechanics, is a fresh look at the foundations of conventional quantum mechanics and is extensible to completely new forms of interactions and models in experimental settings.

papers.title: Better Batches, Better Privacy: Random Allocation for DP-BandMF
papers.abstract: The current state of the art for batch selection and noise addition in differentially private training is a combination of DP Banded Matrix Factorization (DP-BandMF; informally, DP-SGD where the noise added in two different steps can be correlated if the steps are within $b$ of each other) and privacy amplification by sampling via Monte Carlo accounting. First, whereas prior batch selection strategies for DP-BandMF were inspired by Poisson sampling, random allocation is known to outperform Poisson sampling for DP-SGD. We therefore propose and analyze new batch selection strategies for DP-BandMF inspired by random allocation, improving RMSE by up to $1.85\times$ over previous work. Second, Monte Carlo accounting typically requires drawing $\Omega(1/\delta)$ samples from a privacy loss distribution, making accounting costly. We increase sampling and scoring throughput by two orders of magnitude through a carefully optimized GPU implementation. Finally, previous work chose the DP-BandMF strategy matrix and the batch selection strategy independently. We give a simple framework for choosing these parameters jointly, reducing RMSE by up to $13.4\%$ over fixed strategy matrices.

papers.title: A General Algorithm for Minimal Uncoupled Stress--Strain Calculations of Elastic Constants
papers.abstract: We have developed a general algorithm for constructing the minimum number of strain configurations required to extract second-order elastic constants from first-principles stress-strain calculations without algebraic coupling between the constants targeted for extraction. The method operates on the sparsity structure of the symmetry-reduced elastic stiffness matrix, represented by an auxiliary binary matrix, and generates admissible strain patterns algorithmically rather than prescribing separate strain sets for individual crystal symmetries. Each independent elastic constant is obtained from a single stress component, while additional stress relations generated by the same deformation provide internal consistency checks. Because the six-dimensional strain space contains only 2^6-1=63 non-empty strain patterns, the minimality of the resulting sets can be verified exactly for every elastic-symmetry type considered. The construction reproduces established high-efficiency strain sets in cases where they are minimal and yields improved sets for symmetry classes in which previously tabulated schemes require additional configurations. Because the formulation is based on stress-strain derivatives, it can also be readily extended to finite temperatures using consistently sampled ensemble-averaged thermodynamic stresses. Explicit strain sets are derived for all elastic-symmetry types spanning the 230 crystallographic space groups, and their accuracy and computational efficiency are benchmarked against established approaches.

papers.title: Where Can a Decision Model Diagnose HVAC Faults? Reasoning Demand, Physical Representation, and Robustness Under Shift
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence supports building operations in several forms, each with its own barrier. Expert rules must be tuned for every system, supervised models need labeled data that buildings rarely record, and language models return free text that requires human-in-the-loop checking, since their stated confidence is unreliable. A newer kind of pretrained model, here called a decision model, returns a probability for every allowed answer, so one model could serve many decisions without training. This study answers three open questions for fault diagnosis in heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems: which decisions such a model can make, what input it needs, and whether its probabilities hold when conditions change. On 128 fault days from four public datasets of real equipment, faults are graded by the reasoning their diagnosis demands, with data given raw, as physical features, or with Brick topology. The decision model Jev, open language models, and a supervised model face nine tests that change season, control configuration, or building. Given physical features, Jev and the larger open model diagnosed faults whose evidence one feature carries, but not faults that need operating context. Under shift they kept their accuracy and calibration, while the supervised model lost 0.33 macro-F1 yet led or tied within a building. Their probabilities still needed correction, and detection was weak. The study maps which faults a decision model can diagnose and from what input, and supports a division of work in which code computes the physics and the model ranks candidate faults for an operator.

papers.title: Compositeness and decay properties of the flavor partner of $D^{*}_{s0}(2317)$
papers.abstract: In view of the recent experimental finding of the heavy quark flavor partner of the $D_{s0}(2317)$ in the bottom sector, the $B_{s0}(5700)$, we perform a single and coupled-channel $B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{(*)}$ calculation in the hidden-gauge formalism within the on-shell and off-shell schemes, respectively. By fixing the $B\bar{K}$ bound state mass to the observed state with $J^P=0^+$, we also predict five new states with $J^P=\lbrace 0,1,2\rbrace^+$ in this sector, three of them with $J^P=1^+$. Additionally, in the coupled-channel calculation, two states with masses and decay widths similar to the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ and $B_{sJ}(6063)$ ones, with spins $J=0^+$ and $2^+$, respectivley, and decaying into $B\bar{K}$, are dynamically generated. Moreover, we evaluate the decay widths of the $B_{s0}$ and $B_{s1}$ states generated from $B^{(*)}\bar{K}$ through the isospin breaking decay mode $B_s^0\pi^0$ and $B_s^{*0}\pi^0$, respectively. We find that, because these states have large binding energies, the coupling to the bare component can reduce this decay width by more than half of the decay width, from $50$~keV in the purely molecular model to $10-20$~keV, when the $B_{s0}$ is coupled to the bare component. We also observe that, after considering heavy-quark-spin symmetry violating contributions, the decay width for the $B_{s1}$ becomes smaller than for the $B_{s0}$.

papers.title: Public Battery Field Data
papers.abstract: Battery systems and algorithms are developed and evaluated primarily on laboratory cycling data, but fielded battery systems are subjected to duty cycles, temperatures, and measurement conditions that cannot be reproduced in a lab. Field data from batteries in service has begun to appear in public releases attached to individual papers, but each release has its own format, units, labels, and other gaps that make it difficult to compare against others. We present a curated collection of 37 public field-data releases from 28 research groups, covering applications that span passenger EVs, buses, light electric mobility, grid-scale storage, distributed storage, consumer electronics, industrial robotics and satellites. Where the releases are complete enough to measure, this heterogeneous collection contains 256 GB of data from at least 150,626 lithium-ion cells, 3,287 batteries, 115.6 MWh of energy storage capacity, and 3,040 unit-years of service. Critically, it also contains 957 labeled or reported faults, which provide greater visibility into what real battery performance and safety issues look like outside the lab. We release a public repository of metadata and code for each of the field datasets. For each dataset it provides a registry entry with sources, license and access links, checksums to confirm a download is complete, a metadata table, and code for how to load it. We also report where released datasets differ from their papers. We hope the collection can help serve researchers (human or otherwise) as a useful platform for improving battery field diagnostics, fault detection and health estimation. Better field evidence can also feed back to improve manufacturing quality, inform second-life screening and residual-value estimates, and broadly accelerate electrification.

papers.title: Closing the Accuracy Gap in Stochastic First-Order Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic first-order complexity of smooth nonconvex-strongly-convex bilevel optimization with fresh, conditionally unbiased gradient samples of bounded variance. We assume globally $L$-Lipschitz gradients, bounded $f_y$, $\mu$-strong convexity of the lower objective, and $\rho$-Lipschitz lower Hessian blocks. Let $\kappa=L/\mu$, $\vartheta=\rho/\mu$, and $\chi=1+\vartheta$. For $\kappa\ge2$, $1\le\vartheta\le\kappa^2$, every initial-gap budget $\Delta>0$, and $0<\epsilon\le c\min\{L,\sqrt{L\Delta}\}$, we establish $\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{SFO}}(\epsilon)=\widetilde{\Theta}(L\chi\kappa^{5/2}\Delta\epsilon^{-2}+L\kappa^4\sigma_f^2\Delta\epsilon^{-4}+L^3\vartheta^2\chi\kappa^8\sigma_g^2\Delta\epsilon^{-6})$, where $\sigma_f^2$ and $\sigma_g^2$ are the upper- and lower-level variance budgets. The comparison assumes a finite lower-initialization certificate, holds uniformly over both nonnegative noise budgets, and uses an accuracy constant $c$ independent of conditioning. Three lower-bound families capture the deterministic, upper-noise, and lower-noise contributions. The bounds cover arbitrary randomized adaptive queries and terminal outputs under worst-case expected costs, even for conservative sample gradients. The upper bound combines accelerated frozen-linear-tilt solves with displacement-based reuse of the full upper gradient. An independently chosen base-chain length yields the uniform accuracy range, while a projection and homotopy argument separates undisclosed coordinates from a newly disclosed source, allowing $\vartheta/\kappa$ to grow without bound. The bounds match polynomial orders and noise transitions; exact logarithmic exponents and coarser accuracies remain open.

papers.title: VisionQ: Benchmarking VLM Judges on Criterion-Specific Comparisons of Computer Vision Method Outputs
papers.abstract: Qualitative comparison figures in computer vision papers are commonly established to illustrate which method's output is best on a named criterion, such as visual sharpness or surface complexity. VisionQ investigates this important part of computer vision work beyond human judgment towards objective vision-language models (VLMs) as judges. From 1,409 CVPR and ICCV papers, it creates blind multiple-choice questions, each testing one criterion, with the correct answer based on the authors' claimed best result. The best of 21 judges aligns with the authors' claims on 69% of questions, against 32% by chance. Yet it keeps most of its accuracy without the criterion and changes its answers when the options are reordered. Trained on every option order of a larger question set, our VisionQ-Judge raises accuracy on unseen papers from 50% to 61%. The paper highlights the potential of VLM judges to provide objective, criterion-specific comparisons across a broad range of computer vision methods in the past, present, and future. Data, weights and code are available at this https URL and this https URL .

papers.title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
papers.abstract: Evaluating AI agents on scientific research tasks is constrained by the time and resources required for the underlying experiments or calculations. In computational materials research, repeating the same expensive simulations across agents and trials can make evaluation impractical. We introduce CompMat-Bench, a benchmark of 94 tasks derived from recently published computational materials studies, each asking agents to complete a step toward achieving the study's scientific goal. We reproduce the research steps in advance and assess agents on preparing inputs and analyzing outputs for expensive simulations, so expensive simulations can be avoided during evaluation. The reproduced inputs and results serve as ground truth for grading agents with fixed rules, without an LLM judge. We extend the benchmark to four evaluation conditions: single tasks and workflows composed of related tasks, each with full or reduced methodological guidance. In a workflow, the agent runs all simulations itself. With full guidance on single tasks, agents based on nine LLMs demonstrate the ability to complete individual materials research steps, with pass rates of 62.8-97.9% across 94 tasks. Both longer workflows and reduced guidance can limit agent performance, but in different ways for different agents: they lower the pass rates of the weaker agents, whereas the stronger agents fall only when a long workflow is combined with reduced guidance. Failure analysis attributes more failures to scientific errors than to errors in software usage. CompMat-Bench provides a basis for comparing agents on the steps of real materials research and for analyzing agent failure modes.

papers.title: RNA Design via Conditioned Flow Matching and Finite-Policy Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: RNA design aims to identify sequences that fold into specified secondary structures. Existing methods formulate the task as target-specific search or conditional generation. However, natural RNA evolution proceeds through sequence variation and selection, with compensatory substitutions, whereas these methods do not explicitly model this process. To address this limitation, we propose a two-stage framework comprising RNA Inverse-Folding Flow (RNA-IFlow) and RNA-IFlow-RL. RNA-IFlow uses structure-conditioned Dirichlet Flow Matching to model coordinated variation across the sequence, while RNA-IFlow-RL maps the learned flow to a pairing-preserving finite policy and refines it with thermodynamic feedback. Our framework achieves leading performance on multiple benchmarks, reaching 85.19% Pass@1 on Rfam-27. Further analyses reveal thermodynamic gains, policy dynamics, and robustness across settings. Our work couples coordinated variation with thermodynamic selection, offering a novel paradigm for RNA design.

papers.title: Large-scale factor analysis shows machine intelligence is only partially interpretable
papers.abstract: A common assumption in language model development is that cognitive abilities are organized around a general, domain-free intelligence factor, like fluid intelligence in humans. This assumption is rarely tested directly, and prior attempts have done so only at a much smaller scale. We take a latent variable approach to intelligence in language models, similar to how psychometricians study psychological constructs. Using factor analysis, we analyzed 13,230 published evaluation scores covering 1,618 language models across 456 text-only benchmarks. Because the data are sparse, we triangulate our analysis across different data densifiers and imputation methods. Across the imputations that pass our quality filter, the general factor's share of variance in the summed score ($\omega_h$) ranges from 0.04 to 0.76, and its share of the common variance (ECV) from 0.11 to 0.52. A robust pattern across different modes of bias is that 1. same-subject benchmarks are not guaranteed to place closely in vector space, with weak median label cohesion, 2. benchmarks loading highest on $G$ tend to be miscellaneous rather than thematically coherent, and 3. standard "intelligence" benchmarks do not dominate the share of ability variance the general factor explains, and there is a lack of evidence that $G$ is well-proxied by them. We hypothesize that targeting a single conceptual ability has little support, since the first-order abilities it would have to reach are often partially idiosyncratic and not identifiable in practice. This would mean that, from public benchmark scores alone, general intelligence is hard to define, identify, and target as a single construct in language model development. Future experiments should run training regimes that target both theoretically abstract general ability and tasks with semantic similarity and examine how abilities transfer across test sets of diverse formats.

papers.title: Twisted Cohomology of D-Brane Disk Integrals
papers.abstract: Disk-level scattering amplitudes involving one Ramond--Ramond and two NSNS states on a D-brane obey nontrivial identities among scalar world-sheet integrals imposed by gauge and T-duality Ward identities. We investigate the cohomological organization of these relations using twisted de Rham cohomology and show that the Ward identities admit twisted-exact representatives. In the $I/J$ sector, the unique generic linear dependence among the Ward identities is realized one degree lower in the same twisted de Rham complex, revealing a common cohomological origin for the identities and their syzygy. We also identify independent pointwise algebraic relations among the integrands. An independent cohomological rank computation then establishes that the physically selected $I/J$ family spans a five-dimensional subspace of the top twisted cohomology at generic complexified kinematics. Extending the construction to the $K$-family, including the exceptional double-pole representative $K_3$, introduces no additional cohomology direction. For a D1-brane amplitude, we exhibit a physical polarization component in which six scalar periods reduce to one at special kinematics.

papers.title: The long period radio transient ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable
papers.abstract: Wide-field time-domain radio surveys have recently unveiled a new class of Galactic radio emitter: long period radio transients (LPTs). Despite the rapid pace of discovery, their origins remain poorly understood, with two main theories emerging: slowly spinning magnetars or binary white dwarfs (WDs) with magnetic interactions. All three LPTs with well-characterised optical counterparts are WDs in binary systems, but even within that class there is diversity, with one accreting and two detached systems. In this Letter, we show that the LPT ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable (CV)---a WD accreting from a low-mass companion---with a spectroscopic orbital period consistent with the radio pulse period, and specifically, potentially consistent with being a polar. Unlike the other known LPT CV, ASKAP J1448-68 does not exhibit the He II emission that is a hallmark of magnetic CVs in their high accretion states. We also present new optical time-series and infrared photometric observations, showing flickering at the 10% level and suggesting a possible period bouncer origin. This identification of ASKAP J1448-68 adds to the small sample of characterised LPT counterparts, and shows that LPT emission can persist in an accreting WD binary at a low accretion rate.

papers.title: The Hamilton--Jacobi and Symplectic Analysis for Extended Hořava Gravity
papers.abstract: The Hamilton-Jacobi [HJ] analysis and the Faddeev-Jackiw [FJ] quantization for the linearized, non-projectable $\lambda R$ model, extended by the lowest-order term of Blas, Pujolàs, and Sibiryakov and the higher-order term involving the square of the Cotton tensor, were carried out. The cases $\lambda \neq \frac{1}{3}$ and $\lambda = \frac{1}{3}$ are analyzed. Within the Hamilton-Jacobi framework, we obtain the complete set of Hamiltonians, generalized brackets, fundamental differential, characteristic equations, and gauge transformations of the theory. In the Faddeev-Jackiw framework, a symplectic tensor is constructed from which the fundamental brackets are identified. The HJ and FJ brackets coincide, and from the symplectic tensor, the measure for the quantum path integral is calculated. The differences between the cases $\lambda \neq \frac{1}{3}$ and $\lambda = \frac{1}{3}$ at the quantum path integral are discussed.

papers.title: MUSE spectroscopy of the compact dual AGN in the $z=3.273$ radio-loud gravitational lens MG B2016+112
papers.abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (AGN) are unique laboratories for studying how galaxy mergers trigger accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs). However, only a few dual AGN with projected separations $\lesssim$ 1 kpc at redshifts $z>1$ have been confirmed to date. We present archival MUSE spectroscopy of the three resolved lensed images of the radio-loud type-II system MG B2016+ this http URL $z=3.273$ and at a projected separation of 175 pc, this is the most compact confirmed dual AGN at $z > 1$. We detect Ly$\alpha$, C IV, N V, He II, and C III] emission across images A--C after correcting for ISM absorption at $z \sim 0$. We find that the Ly$\alpha$, C IV, and N V lines are affected by saturated absorption at $z\sim 3.27$. The He II / C III] emission-line ratios are consistent between images A and B but differ significantly from image C. We fit the Ly$\alpha$ and C IV emission regions in images A--C with a broad and a narrow Gaussian and use the broad Gaussian components in C IV to place lower limits on their respective SMBH masses: $\gtrsim 5.5 \times {10}^{6} M_\odot$, $\gtrsim 6.3 \times {10}^{6} M_\odot$, and $\gtrsim 4.8 \times {10}^{6} M_\odot$. We then combine these SMBH mass limits with the magnification-corrected luminosities derived from both the MUSE data and recent Chandra X-ray observations to estimate their Eddington ratios. Our findings motivate deep, spatially resolved near-IR spectroscopy to independently determine the SMBH masses from H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ emission and determine the physical conditions of the host galaxy.

papers.title: Spectral and Polarization Properties of Coherent Radio Emission from Relativistic Magnetized Pair Plasma Shocks
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients whose emission mechanism remains an open question. The so-called synchrotron maser instability in relativistic magnetized shocks is a leading candidate for FRBs produced outside the compact object magnetosphere, yet its spectral and polarization predictions have not been systematically explored. We present three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of relativistic magnetized pair plasma shocks with upstream magnetization $\sigma > 1$ and bulk Lorentz factor $\gamma_0 = 10$, assuming a plane-parallel shock geometry and neglecting radiative cooling, and compute the spectra and polarization of the precursor maser emission for an arbitrary line of sight. For on-axis observers aligned with the shock-propagation direction, the X-mode dominates the emission. The O-mode power increases at off-axis viewing angles and is primarily associated with currents parallel to the upstream background magnetic field. Assuming a spherical shock, we find full-width-at-half-maximum fractional bandwidths of $\Delta\nu/\nu_0\simeq0.57$ and $0.82$ for $\sigma=3$ and $6$, respectively. For highly magnetized shocks, the intrinsic emission bandwidth accounts for most of the spectral width, while high-latitude contributions provide additional broadening. The integrated emission remains highly linearly polarized near the spectral peak, with a nearly constant polarization angle due to the dominance of the X-mode. Our results suggest that synchrotron maser emission can produce spectra with bandwidths and high linear polarization degrees compatible with observations of some non-repeating FRBs, and may provide testable signatures for distinguishing shock-powered FRBs from other emission mechanisms.

papers.title: A Peterson program for general Schubert varieties and mirror symmetry
papers.abstract: We initiate a `Peterson program' that seeks to extend Dale Peterson's theory for the quantum cohomology of flag varieties to arbitrary Schubert varieties, and that incorporates a mirror-symmetric approach. In this first paper we introduce a generalisation of the (localised) Peterson variety associated to an arbitrary Schubert variety $\check X_{w,P}$ inside a partial flag variety $\check G/\check P$. This generalisation is possibly a non-reduced affine scheme that lies in the Langlands dual full flag variety $G/B$. Additionally, we construct a Lie-theoretic `superpotential' associated to $\check X_{w,P}$, generalising earlier ones for the flag varieties $\check G/\check P$ from [Rie08], and we show that its relative critical point locus recovers the generalised Peterson variety. We make the key conjecture that for smooth Fano Schubert varieties the coordinate ring of the generalised Peterson variety recovers the quantum cohomology ring of $\check X_{w,P}$ localised at the quantum parameters. For smooth Fano Schubert varieties $X_{w,B}$ in $\check G/\check B$ we furthermore map our generalised Peterson variety to the cotangent bundle $\mathcal T^*(T)$ of the maximal torus $T$ of $G$ and construct a partial compactification that we conjecture models the full quantum cohomology ring of $\check X_{w,B}$, in analogy with the Givental-Kim presentation of $QH^*(\check G/\check B)$ via the degenerate leaf of the Kostant Toda lattice of $\check G$. These conjectures are verified for all smooth Schubert divisors in the complete type $A$ flag variety, and we show that our superpotential agrees with that introduced for Grassmannian Schubert varieties by Rietsch and Williams, after a suitable isomorphism of the domains.

papers.title: Quantized response of amplification in non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystals
papers.abstract: Photonic time crystals amplify waves through periodic temporal modulation of the permittivity. We study a non-Hermitian photonic time quasicrystal, a temporal analogue of the non-Hermitian Aubry-Andre-Harper model of quasiperiodic lattices. Its modulation is incommensurate and has a complex phase, whose imaginary part, the complexification parameter, acts as an imaginary gauge field on the modulation harmonics. We find that the bulk amplification rate, as a function of this parameter, is organized into distinct phases, within each of which its slope is locked to an integer, known in quasiperiodic operator theory as Avila's acceleration. The phase boundaries are predicted from Fourier coefficients of rational approximants and confirmed by transfer-matrix and time-domain simulations. Under analytic distortions of the modulation waveform, the integer phases persist while their boundaries move. Consequently, two input frequencies in different integer phases have an amplification ratio that varies exponentially with the complexification parameter, which enables spectral selection. These results establish a topologically protected, quantized response law for amplification in such time-varying media.

papers.title: StAGE: Stellar Archaeology-driven Galaxy Evolution II. Binary Black Hole Mergers in Quiescent Galaxies and their Star-forming Progenitors
papers.abstract: We apply StAGE, a data-driven galaxy-evolution framework based on stellar archaeology, to study binary black hole (BBH) mergers associated with present-day quiescent galaxies (QGs) and their star-forming progenitors. By combining StAGE star-formation and chemical-enrichment histories with pre-computed SEVN population-synthesis catalogs, we predict the BBH merger-rate density, intrinsic binary properties, merger-time host-galaxy distributions, and the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) background. A distinctive feature of StAGE is that it jointly tracks the stellar-binary environment at birth and the properties of the host galaxy at merger time. Moreover, stellar-archaeology constraints on $\alpha$-enhancement allow us to explore how adopting the iron abundance relevant for massive-star winds, rather than oxygen-based total metallicity, affects the predicted BBH merger rates. We find that most BBHs form at moderately subsolar metallicities $Z\lesssim Z_\odot/3$, while their merger-time hosts typically have stellar masses $M_\star\sim10^{10}-10^{11.5}\,M_\odot$ at $z\lesssim2$. At and beyond cosmic noon, hosts lie mainly on the star-forming main sequence, whereas starbursting and quenching descendants contribute increasingly toward lower redshift. Using the independent approach offered by StAGE, we also confirm recent literature findings that, for most binary-evolution prescriptions, predicted local BBH merger rates exceed the LVK-inferred range, while dynamical formation in stellar clusters extends the BBH primary mass distribution into the high-mass regime poorly populated by isolated binaries. Finally, the predicted stochastic background approaches the projected sensitivity of planned LVK upgrades and lies within reach of the Einstein Telescope. All in all, StAGE can provide physically motivated host priors for GW-source localization and dark-siren cosmology.

papers.title: Global Exponential and Inverse Optimal Stabilization of a 3D Nonholonomic Vehicle in Spherical Coordinates
papers.abstract: For the 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated in surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate, we construct continuous time-invariant feedback laws that stabilize both the roll-free and roll-augmented kinematic models to a target position and orientation in spherical coordinates. The design uses a spherical coordinate transformation with a singular set of codimension two and measure zero. We first present a backstepping design that yields explicit unidirectional, cusp-free feedback laws and strict barrier control Lyapunov functions (CLFs). These establish global exponential stability in spherical coordinates with user-assigned decay rates, while ensuring bounded Cartesian trajectories and exponential convergence to the target, consistent with Brockett's obstruction. The barrier terms guarantee avoidance of the coordinate singularities away from the target. The strict CLFs are then used to develop families of asymptotically stabilizing inverse optimal feedback laws for both systems that minimize a meaningful infinite-horizon cost. These laws inherit infinite gain margins from driftlessness, respect user-defined input bounds through Legendre-Fenchel transformations, and are implementable with either bidirectional or unidirectional surge actuation. Two penalty choices are illustrated: a quadratic input penalty whose associated state running cost approaches a prescribed quadratic form, and an input-constraining penalty that enforces user-defined bounds. This paper lays the foundation for constructive stabilization of the 3D nonholonomic vehicle.

papers.title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, $q$ being a prime power. For an entanglement-assisted or unassisted stabilizer code defined by an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear space $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$, a set of erasures and an associated repair group, we propose a procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures, within the stabilizer measurement model. The repair group is reduced by eliminating qudits that need not be measured. In classical local recovery, such symbols can be found by Gaussian elimination, although the resulting repair group need not be a smallest one. In the quantum case we eliminate an admissible set of qudits. Finding a largest admissible set is a linear matroid parity problem, and for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes defined by two linear codes it is a linear matroid intersection problem. Both problems are solvable in deterministic polynomial time. We give closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for general codes and for codes from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and, for two-code CSS codes, a sharper bound with a min--max formula. Based on these bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the concept of dimension locality of classical local recovery.

papers.title: Discrete-time Kuramoto model with phase lag: Linear stability analysis and onset of synchronization
papers.abstract: We investigate the discrete-time version of the Kuramoto model with phase lag, which comprises globally-coupled phase oscillators of distributed frequencies that are evolving under a nonlinear map. In the continuum limit of an infinite number of oscillators ($N\to \infty$), we derive the exact Frobenius-Perron equation for the time evolution of the single-oscillator probability density, and study linear stability of the incoherent state. Instability signals onset of synchronization. The corresponding synchronization threshold is obtained analytically for the case of a Lorentzian distribution of the oscillator frequencies. The threshold differs from that of the continuous-time Kuramoto model, reflecting the fundamentally different stability conditions for discrete-time maps and continuous-time flows. Beyond synchronization threshold, we observe several interesting nonlinear phenomena: Unlike the classical Kuramoto model, the discrete-time version exhibits periodic and chaotic states. Numerical simulations of the finite-$N$ system confirm the analytical prediction for the synchronization threshold, while highlighting breakdown of the celebrated Ott-Antonsen ansatz invoked to conveniently study the continuous-time Kuramoto model in terms of a low-dimensional description.

papers.title: Stoic Logic and Natural Term Logic
papers.abstract: In this paper we propose a reconstruction of Stoic Logic focused on the aspect of multiple generality using the Natural Term Logic (NTL) developped by the author in \cite{ntl}. It can be shown, based on the available evidence, that Stoic logic was far more than a mere propositional logic (we cannot simply identiify the Stoic conditional with propositional conditionals). Its more general and complex logical theory - and notable the treatment of multiple generality - was rather patterned after the logico-syntactic mechanisms of natural language (subject to a regimentation which recalls Polish notation). NTL is likewise is a variable-free formal framework which captures the core syntactic and logic mechanisms of natural language (and notably a large array of features involving intensionality and anaphoric constructions). Bobzien and Shogry \cite{bobzienshogry} have argued that quantified conditionals and multiple generality were treated by the Stoics through a disambiguifying regimentation of syntax using indefinite pronouns and anaphoric constructions involving such pronouns. We contend that the quantified condition expressed through an anaphoric construction involving indefinite pronouns is the fundamental building block of ancient logic. And we explore some possible building blocks for a formal reconstruction of the Stoic logic of universal conditionals (and its corresponding general form of Stoic modus ponens attested by ancient authors) based on NTL. More specifically, we present a version of NTL in which the anaphoric constructions of the Stoic quantified conditional correspond to a type of primitive constructor. The constructor also has a remarkable graph-theoretic interpretation which gives this version of NTL interest in its own right.

papers.title: Electrostatic Stabilization of Near-Surface Quantum Sensors via Dielectric Interface Engineering
papers.abstract: Control of charge-state stability in near-surface quantum defects is critical for nanoscale sensing, yet remains particularly challenging under ultra-high vacuum (UHV), where surface-induced band bending destabilizes the metrologically relevant charge-state. Here, we present a robust and reproducible approach for stabilizing shallowly implanted (< 10 nm deep) nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in near-UHV conditions (P = $3 \times 10^{-9}$ mbar) based on dielectric interface engineering. Through measurements on individually addressable NV centers, we demonstrate that a TiO2 coating on the diamond suppresses surface-induced electrostatic fields, yielding a 79% increase n NV- population and a 45% enhancement in NV-spin resonance contrast at room temperature. Coherent control measurements further reveal suppressed charge-state conversion dynamics. These results establish dielectric screening as a powerful and reproducible strategy to engineer charge transition energetics of NV centers in scanning-probe-compatible geometries under extreme conditions.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents for Evidence Based Genetic Disease Severity Classification
papers.abstract: Disease severity classification for genetic conditions is subjective and labor-intensive, creating bottlenecks in genomic screening, where commercial panels vary widely in size and overlap. We developed an autonomous AI agent integrating Reasoning and Acting (ReAct) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to classify 10,211 Human Phenotype Ontology terms. It uses American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG)-endorsed severity guidelines and American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) quality-of-life criteria to retrieve PubMed literature, generate interpretable reasoning chains, and independently verify claims. At the phenotype level, using expert-curated cohorts, the agent achieved 93.55% accuracy (MCC 0.9237) with 82.6% to 91.4% of claims supported by direct evidence or valid inferences. Gene-level severity was aggregated across 8,738 pairs, identifying 3,283 autosomal recessive pairs with severe or profound presentations. External validation showed 95.2% concordance with Mackenzie's Mission gene list. This system enables standardized panel design by providing reliable, automated classification supported by direct evidence.

papers.title: Canonical and symplectic analysis of the Holst action in the $G\rightarrow 0$ limit
papers.abstract: By using the Dirac and symplectic formalisms, the analysis of the Holst action in the $G \rightarrow 0$ limit is performed. We study the theory's full canonical structure and symmetries. In particular, we focus on the cases $\gamma = i$ and $\gamma \neq i$, aiming to obtain Smolin's auto-self-dual model in terms of the Ashtekar variables and a Barbero-type formulation. We then perform the symplectic analysis and discuss the principal insight of these formalisms.

papers.title: Radiation Magneto-hydrodynamic Simulations of MRI with Zero-Net-Vertical-Flux: Necessity of Resolving the Thermal Scale For Strongly Magnetized Initial Conditions
papers.abstract: We perform 3D radiation magneto-hydrodynamic (RMHD) shearing-box simulations of local patches of optically thick accretion disks, applicable to sub-Eddington active galactic nuclei (AGN) at $\sim 1000$ gravitational radii around a supermassive black hole (SMBH) of $10^7-10^8M_\odot$. In particular, we set up zero-net-vertical-flux (ZNVF) simulations with strong net azimuthal fields ($B_y$) characterized by initial gas-to-magnetic pressure ratio $\beta_0$. We find that $\beta_0 \sim 1$ simulations relax to the classical MRI state with steady-state $\beta\sim 10-20$ and slow periodic reversals of the mean azimuthal field (dynamo cycles), losing memory of their initial $B_y$ configuration. The outcome of simulations starting from $\beta_0=0.1$ (superthermal magnetic pressures) depends upon the numerical resolution as quantified by the number of grid cells per thermal scale height $H_\mathrm{th}$. Resolved simulations ($\Delta z\le H_\mathrm{th}/5$) settle into final states similar to the larger-$\beta_0$ runs, exhibiting thermally dominated midplanes heated by MRI turbulence and undergoing dynamo cycles. In contrast, lower resolution $\beta_0 = 0.1$ runs evolve towards states dominated by a coherent mean field, similar to what is observed in recent isothermal MHD simulations. However, those disks fail to sustain sufficient turbulent heating near the midplane and undergo runaway cooling and contraction. While such states might be sustained in global models with even lower initial $\beta_0$ and/or continuous $B_y$ injection, our results indicate that they could arise purely from under-resolving the midplane MRI dynamo that would otherwise be able to generate and emanate randomized fields. We highlight the need to resolve a fraction of the thermal scale height (the classical MRI wavelengths) for strongly magnetized initial conditions to obtain converged outcomes in RMHD simulations.

papers.title: 1/f frequency noise in mechanical resonators scales inversely with volume, not with quality factor
papers.abstract: Mechanical frequency-shift sensors have never reached the resolution their thermomechanical or quantum limits predict: a $1/f$ frequency-noise floor keeps them 1-4 orders short of it. Across the published record, the product of the floor's flicker coefficient $h_{-1}$ and the strain-weighted resonator volume, $V_{\varepsilon}$, is size-independent over 13 decades. It is also independent of measured $Q$; I find that $Q$-volume covariance underlies reported $Q$-dependence. It is defect density that imposes the frequency-noise floor: prestress can dilute it, but only in fixed-end devices. Mass resolution follows as $|\delta m|\propto\sqrt{V}$.

papers.title: Who Wrote This? Turing, Total Variation, and the Mathematics of AI-Text Detection
papers.abstract: What can a finished text reveal about the process that produced it? Drawing on Turing's imitation game and statistical decision theory, this article examines the limits of AI-text detection as an inference from a completed object to an unobserved history. For two known source distributions with equal prior probabilities, a standard identity gives the minimum average classification error as half their probability overlap. This overlap is one minus their total variation distance. Perfect detection therefore requires nonoverlapping distributions; useful discrimination does not. In practice, the problem is harder: human and machine writing form changing families of distributions, posterior probabilities depend on base rates, and ``AI-written'' becomes ambiguous when people and software contribute to the same text. Turing's interrogator can ask another question; a detector restricted to finished prose cannot. Distinguishability, source attribution, authentication, and compliance are different inferential tasks. The paper's own documented human-AI provenance shows what a production history can reveal that a binary label cannot.

papers.title: Infinite twisted $C^*$-tensor product and symmetric states
papers.abstract: The twisted $C^*$-tensor product was exhaustively investigated by the authors in two previous papers. In this new context, generalising the usual tensor product and the Fermi one, we analyse the possibility of studying the set of symmetric states, that is those invariant under all finite permutations, in the setting of infinite twisted $C^*$-tensor products. As a preliminary result, we recognise that such an investigation can proceed only when the bicharacter, involved in the construction of such twisted tensor products, is hermitian. Otherwise, there is no natural action of the finitary symmetric group on the infinite twisted chain. Furthermore, even if the investigation of symmetric states is certainly meaningful for all twisted systems based on hermitian bicharacters, it is shown that it can be fruitfully carried out in three cases only. In these cases, we can provide the "genuine" version of the celebrated De Finetti Theorem already established by Hewitt and Savage for the general classical case, Stormer for the usual tensor product and Fidaleo for Fermi models. Very surprisingly, it emerges that one more twisted model can be treated exhaustively: it corresponds to the chain twisted by the so-called Klein four-group, and its Klein bicharacter unique up to equivalence.

papers.title: Electron Spin Pumping by Thermal Radiation
papers.abstract: This Letter demonstrates that thermal radiation can pump angular momentum into the spins of itinerant electrons across a vacuum gap, without spatial spin transport or net charge flow. In a monolayer transition metal dichalcogenide radiatively coupled to a thermal emitter, Rashba spin-orbit coupling enables spin-selective transitions between helical conduction bands. Two distinct mechanisms are identified: chiral spin pumping mediated by interference between polarization components of thermal radiation from a nonreciprocal emitter, and nonchiral spin pumping arising from Zeeman-induced asymmetry between opposing spin-flip transitions driven by nonchiral thermal fluctuations.

papers.title: Interstellar Complex Organic Molecules and Molecular Outflows in NGC 1333 IRAS 4B and 4B' Observed Using NOEMA
papers.abstract: We present interferometric observations with the Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA) of NGC 1333 IRAS 4B and 4B', two young stellar objects (YSOs) within the Perseus molecular cloud. YSOs, especially Class 0 protostars, are rich in gas-phase interstellar complex organic molecules (iCOMs), but relatively little is known about the spatial distribution of these important prebiotic molecules. Various molecules were imaged within IRAS 4B and the surrounding area in the 145 GHz spectral range, revealing hundreds of molecular transitions within the warm inner envelope of IRAS 4B. This work provides derived physical parameters (rotational temperature, column density, velocity shift with respect to local standard of rest, and full-width at half-maximum spectral line width) for 11 molecules toward IRAS 4B including methanol (CH$_3$OH and isotopologues), methyl formate (HCOOCH$_3$), dimethyl ether (CH$_3$OCH$_3$), acetaldehyde (CH$_3$CHO), ethanol (C$_2$H$_5$OH), glycolaldehyde (CH$_2$OHCHO), acetone (CH$_3$COCH$_3$), and isocyanic acid (HNCO). Out of these molecules, 10 are iCOMs (excluding HNCO) that trace the inner envelope of IRAS 4B and mark it as a rich source of organic material. There is a strong spatial correlation between the continuum emission of IRAS 4B and iCOM molecular emission and among various iCOMs with each other. Physical parameter and integrated intensity maps show that IRAS 4B is a binary protostar system that drives a jet in a north-south orientation and an outflow in a northwest-southeast orientation. IRAS 4B' also drives a west-east outflow but shows no evidence of molecular emission cospatial with its continuum emission.
